| **DL-77** | **Resolves OD-46 in full. Urgency is the maximum interruption entitlement Operational Trust grants to a Communication, on a fixed, cumulative, four-level ladder — No Interruption, Interrupt Current Activity, Override Protected Time, Wake or Disturb — risk-informed but formally independent of DL-76 Action-Risk Classification, never overriding audience, privacy, consent, disclosure, identity, authority, precedence, or life-safety governance** (P15, P26, P27, P30, P32, DL-03, DL-21, DL-26, DL-27, DL-28, DL-29, DL-34, DL-36, DL-37, DL-39, DL-40, DL-53, DL-75, DL-76). **1. Definition.** Urgency answers *"what may this Communication interrupt now?"* — never Category, severity, a delivery surface, a delivery command, precedence, retry, escalation, audience, permission to disclose, an originator assertion, or a requirement that Concierge use the maximum permitted interruption. The originator may propose; **Operational Trust determines and grants**. **2. The canonical ladder.** Exactly four levels, cumulative, each a maximum permitted interruption, never a mandatory delivery behaviour: **No Interruption** (retained, presented when context permits, may not interrupt a current activity, active Mode, protected time, or a sleeping person); **Interrupt Current Activity** (adds: may interrupt a current activity or active Mode when other governance permits; may not override protected time or wake/disturb merely by this level); **Override Protected Time** (adds: may override quiet hours or another governed protected-time condition when other governance permits; may not wake/disturb merely by this level); **Wake or Disturb** (adds: may wake or deliberately disturb the intended audience when all other governance permits). **3. Category remains orthogonal**, restating the existing, un-reopened `communication.md` rule — neither determines the other, and the two are never merged into one enumeration, score, or platform ladder. **4. Relationship to DL-76.** Urgency and Action-Risk Classification are independent models evaluated by Operational Trust; DL-76's Risk Class, defaults, thresholds, threshold crossings, and configuration are consumed as **one input among several**; there is no required one-to-one mapping, and two circumstances sharing a Risk Class may receive different Urgency because current facts, context, audience, or configuration differ. **5. Originator proposal.** Optional, advisory, never the granted entitlement merely because proposed, never prescriptive of surface or timing, never able to bypass Operational Trust; Operational Trust determines Urgency when no proposal exists, and the absence is itself recorded. **6. Six distinct values, never collapsed into one field:** **Originator Proposal** (the optional proposed level); **Canonical HTBW Recommendation** (the current baseline recommendation for the governed scenario or configuration scope); **Learned Household Recommendation** (see section 9); **Configured Value** (the value currently accepted for the applicable scope); **Household Override State** (whether the configured value differs from the applicable recommendation, with provenance); **Granted Runtime Entitlement** (the entitlement Operational Trust grants after evaluating configured policy and current facts). **7. Recommended-value and override pattern.** HTBW provides a recommended setting wherever evidence supports one; the household must be able to view every canonical level, see HTBW's recommendation, accept it, choose another, see override status, and understand the consequence — visibility and explicit choice are canonical, a specific UI control is not. **8. Configurable determination rules.** The four-level ladder is fixed; the rules determining which level is granted are configuration within existing HTBW authority, evaluating Risk Class, thresholds, asset-class and individual-asset policy, household defaults and overrides, current state and context, active Mode, protected time, presence, audience eligibility, identity confidence, consent, privacy, disclosure policy, and escalation state — **never a blind numeric calculation**, and configuration may never bypass audience, privacy, consent, disclosure, identity, authority, or life-safety governance. **9. Learned Household Recommendations reuse the existing P26/DL-21 learning promotion ladder (`behavioral-governance.md`), governed by OD-28 — no new learning or recommendation mechanism is created.** A Learned Household Recommendation is a Suggestion-stage proposal whose subject is an Urgency default, exactly as **DL-75** established for Significance: the canonical HTBW Recommendation remains permanently, separately identifiable; no configured value changes silently; the pattern supporting the recommendation is explainable; an authorized identity must explicitly accept it before it changes configuration; rejection never alters current configuration; and acceptance, rejection, and reset are governed Change Records under the existing promotion-ladder discipline. **10. Reset to the HTBW baseline extends DL-76's existing three-tier override model (Capability Default → HTBW Default → Household Override) with an explicit Reset action**, never a new mechanism: reset shows the proposed changes, requires a sufficiently identified and authorized actor and explicit confirmation, removes the Household Override and any unaccepted Learned Household Recommendation within the selected scope, and restores the Configured Value to the Canonical HTBW Recommendation — available at whatever configuration scopes DL-76's own override model already supports. **Reset never rewrites history**: prior values, prior determinations, and the reset decision itself remain explainable through existing versioning, Change Records, and the Decision Trace. **11. Urgency may be reevaluated.** Operational Trust reevaluates the granted entitlement when material inputs change — facts, risk evaluation, threshold state, escalation state, configuration, audience, presence, active Mode, protected-time status, or other relevant context. **A reevaluation is a new Operational Trust determination. It is never automatically retry, and never automatically escalation.** Elapsed time alone is never sufficient to increase Urgency absent an accepted threshold, policy, risk change, or escalation rule that makes it materially relevant. **12. Effect of a decrease.** Pending delivery must immediately respect the new, lower entitlement; completed delivery remains historical fact and is never rewritten; queued delivery or retry requiring the former entitlement is cancelled or replanned; stale interruption rights are never used; the reevaluation, the prior entitlement, the new entitlement, and the resulting action remain explainable. **13. Precedence remains OD-04's.** Urgency grants interruption eligibility; it does not order Communications that are otherwise eligible. **OD-04 owns relative precedence**, including the ordering of Communications sharing one Urgency level; this decision creates no second precedence score, timestamp rule, or hidden tie-breaker. **14. Audience governance is never overridden.** Guest eligibility, and every other audience question, is governed by the Communication's own audience policy (**DL-34**), never by an Urgency exception — a Communication whose governed audience includes all current occupants (a smoke or carbon-monoxide condition) was never granted that audience **by** its Urgency; audience determines who may receive it, disclosure governs what may be revealed, Urgency governs what may be interrupted, and Concierge governs how to help within all three. **15. Privacy, consent, and disclosure are never overridden**, restating **DL-29**, **DL-34**, and **P32** directly: permission to interrupt is not permission to disclose; where the granted entitlement cannot be exercised without violating audience, privacy, consent, or disclosure governance, **delivery degrades** — surface change, content-free Indication where **OD-57**'s own rule permits it, or non-delivery — the governance never does, and both the granted entitlement and the degradation are recorded. **16. Concierge and surface separation.** Urgency sets the maximum; **Concierge decides whether, when, through which surface, and in what form**, operating only within the granted entitlement, the governed audience, privacy/consent/disclosure restrictions, and verified surface capability; Concierge may choose less disruptive delivery than the maximum allowed, may never exceed the granted entitlement, and a material choice to use less than the maximum remains explainable. **17. Delivery Surface capability verification restates DL-53 directly, not reopened**: a surface exercises only capability it can verifiably honour; HTBW distinguishes the canonical entitlement, the verified platform capability, the adapter mapping, unsupported behaviour, and degradation behaviour, and never falsely claims an entitlement was fulfilled. **18. Platform mapping.** HTBW's canonical Urgency determination is mapped downward by the Delivery Surface adapter to a verified platform capability where one exists; the mapping never renames an HTBW level, never treats a platform ladder as the HTBW ladder, never lets a platform severity determine Operational Trust policy, and never lets a platform limitation rewrite the canonical model. **Two existing, unrelated non-Urgency platform severities are reaffirmed, not merged**: the developer-facing three-value `IssueSeverity` (**DL-65**, `home-assistant-boundary.md`), and the Home Assistant 2026.9 Security-dashboard resident-facing, household-declared, two-valued `Alert`/`Warning` presentation severity (`home-assistant-boundary.md` R5) — **neither is adopted as an HTBW Urgency value**; both carry no audience, no entitlement, and no interruption policy. **19. Identity-and-authority-governed deferral is distinct from Urgency, retry, escalation, and acknowledgement, and is not redesigned here.** A deferral request ("remind me in 30 minutes") changes delivery eligibility or timing; it does not itself change the granted Urgency. Not every identified person may defer every Communication: a deferral requires an identified actor, sufficient identity confidence for the requested action, an Operational Trust authority determination, evaluation of whether the Communication type is deferrable and of the requested duration or condition, and an explainable allow-or-deny outcome, recorded with requester, evidence, authority, duration/condition, result, rationale, and start/end or revocation — **this restates, and does not relocate, the existing ownership `stewardship.md` already records** (acknowledgement/snooze/suppression semantics remain **OD-45** and **OD-54**; a later Operational Trust reevaluation may terminate or supersede a deferral where changed facts justify a stronger entitlement). **20. Responsibility boundaries.** Operational Trust owns Urgency recommendation, determination, grant, reevaluation, and authority to accept/override/reset/defer; the originating responsibility owns the Communication, Category, and its optional proposal, never the entitlement, surface, timing, form, or final audience; Identity owns evidence and confidence, never authority; Concierge owns whether/when/surface/form within the entitlement, never Urgency, audience policy, privacy policy, disclosure authority, or Risk Class. **No new Communication, Messaging, Delivery, Escalation, Urgency, Recommendation, or Deferral responsibility is created.** **21. Life-safety boundary**, restating the existing non-negotiable constraint, not reopening **OD-56**: HTBW is not a life-safety system and never describes a Communication as a certified alarm, a guaranteed emergency-warning system, or a substitute for a native smoke, carbon-monoxide, fire, security, or water-shutoff system; HTBW may communicate about native device state or supplement native behaviour, but never suppresses, defers, delays, or replaces a native alarm, and never claims responsibility for native alarm delivery. **22. Explainability** carries, where applicable: the originator proposal or its recorded absence, the canonical recommendation, any learned recommendation, the configured value and override status, the Risk Class and threshold state considered, current facts and context, the audience and Guest-eligibility determination, privacy/consent/disclosure decisions, the granted entitlement and any prior entitlement on reevaluation, determination time, policy and configuration versions, provenance, the selected or degraded surface, deferral state, and the **OD-04** precedence reference — through the existing Decision Trace and temporal/Change Record mechanisms, never a new mechanism. **23. Provenance** reuses existing governed-reference and version-identity mechanisms for every recommendation, configured value, override, reset, and granted entitlement; no arbitrary free-text provenance is introduced where a governed reference is required. **24. Retry and escalation remain exactly as accepted**: repeating delivery to the same audience is retry (Concierge's); escalation changes the accountable audience (**OD-22**'s); a new Urgency determination is, by itself, **neither** — an escalation event may supply changed facts Operational Trust reevaluates, but Urgency never rises merely because a retry occurred. **25. No second store.** Every mechanism above reuses Communications, temporal records, Change Records, version identity, governed references, and the Decision Trace; no Urgency-specific audit log, embedded delivery-history array, independent Communication-history subsystem, or ungoverned recommendation-history store is created | [../models/communication.md](../models/communication.md), [../models/operational-trust.md](../models/operational-trust.md), [../contracts/operational-trust-contract.md](../contracts/operational-trust-contract.md), [../models/glossary.md](../models/glossary.md), [../architecture/home-assistant-boundary.md](../architecture/home-assistant-boundary.md) |
| **DL-78** | **Resolves OD-53 in full. Communication Category is a closed, seven-value, content-domain enumeration — Stewardship, Security, Care, Environment, Experience, System, Safety — identifying what a Communication is about, structurally separate from DL-77 Urgency, Operation Type, DL-76 Action-Risk Classification, and responsibility ownership** (P15, P26, P27, P30, P32, DL-21, DL-26, DL-27, DL-28, DL-29, DL-34, DL-36, DL-76, DL-77). **1. Definition.** Category is Communication metadata identifying the immediate household purpose or content domain; selected by the originator; drawn from the closed canonical enumeration; stable for the Communication's life except under governed correction; an input to downstream governance. **Never** Urgency, severity, priority, interruption entitlement, delivery form, surface, outcome, deferral, retry, escalation, precedence, retention policy, disclosure policy, re-presentation policy, an architectural responsibility, a handling state, an importance label, a platform ladder, or a household-created label. **2. Content-domain, not responsibility-aligned.** The taxonomy is organised around household-facing content domains, never the seven HTBW responsibilities — no Category value named Foundation, Identity, Operational Trust, Continuity, Concierge, Explainability, or Governance may exist merely because that responsibility originated, processed, retained, or delivered the Communication; classification follows what the Communication is immediately about, never which responsibility handled it. **3. The closed canonical enumeration is exactly seven values: Stewardship, Security, Care, Environment, Experience, System, Safety.** Never household-defined, integration-defined, platform-defined, or extensible through ordinary configuration; a new value requires formal governance, repository updates, canonical definitions, boundary analysis, and acceptance review; no free-text value and no local alias becomes canonical; every responsibility consumes the same governed source. **4. Foundation owns** the Category axis in the Communication model, the closed enumeration, canonical definitions, assignment guidance, and the source vocabulary consumed throughout the framework; **Foundation does not own** per-Communication selection, Urgency, disclosure, retention, or re-presentation behaviour. **5. The originating responsibility assigns exactly one Category at creation**, because it owns the Communication's immediate subject and purpose; it never invents a new value, never assigns more than one, never assigns Urgency merely by assigning Category, and never uses Category as a hidden priority or severity value. **6. Operational Trust Category admissibility is rejected.** Operational Trust never approves, rejects, reinterprets, replaces, repairs, or reclassifies a Category, and never determines what a Communication is about; it **consumes** Category as one input among several to disclosure, audience, privacy, consent, Urgency, and other governed-appropriateness decisions — **Operational Trust owns appropriateness, never semantic classification.** The prior "inadmissible Category" scenario is rejected: every originator draws from the identical closed enumeration, so no governed-rejection case exists; an invalid value is a data-integrity defect, never a governed outcome. **7. Exactly one Category per Communication.** No multiple, primary-and-secondary, array, tag, weighted, hierarchical, or compound Category ("Stewardship + Safety") is ever permitted; where a situation touches several domains, the originator selects the one Category stating the Communication's immediate household purpose, and every other relevant fact remains in content, metadata, source references, Decision Trace, or context — never an additional Category. **8. Informational is not a Category.** It names significance, priority, severity, delivery expectation, interruption intent, or presentation style, never a content domain; every Category can contain information, so adopting it would recreate the superseded Info/Attention/Urgent conflation. **9. Advisory is not a Category**, restating the existing, un-reopened rule: a Communication conveying a Stewardship Advisory carries Category = Stewardship, never Category = Advisory. **10. The seven canonical Categories, each with an immediate-purpose test:** **Stewardship** (condition, care, maintenance, obligation, lifecycle, preservation, readiness of assets/systems/spaces — never Safety merely because neglect could eventually raise risk); **Security** (access, intrusion, unauthorised presence, credential compromise, protective controls — distinct from Safety even where a security system supplied the fact); **Care** (personal well-being, health-adjacent matters, medication, wellness, animal well-being — never implying HTBW is a healthcare provider, medical device, or diagnostic system); **Environment** (weather, temperature, humidity, air or water quality as observed condition — never Safety unless the immediate purpose is risk-reducing warning or guidance); **Experience** (comfort, convenience, hospitality, preference, routine, arrival/departure — never a synonym for low Urgency); **System** (technical health, availability, configuration, integration, platform behaviour — distinguished from Stewardship by immediate technical-operation purpose, not by device); **Safety** (conditions, events, warnings, or guidance whose immediate purpose is reducing risk of injury or harm to people, animals, or occupants — establishes no life-safety claim; see section 23). **11. Classification follows immediate household purpose** — never device type alone, the responsibility involved, every possible downstream consequence, current Urgency, severity, delivery method, audience, or platform terminology. Worked distinctions are accepted exactly as specified: smoke detected, carbon monoxide detected, a cougar in the yard, and a dangerous-heat warning for a dog are each **Safety**; replacing a smoke-detector battery and an annual smoke-detector inspection are each **Stewardship**; routine humidity observation is **Environment**. An asset serving a safety purpose does not make all maintenance Communications about it **Safety**. **12. Category is stable for the Communication's life.** An increase in risk, consequence, threshold state, elapsed time, escalation state, or Urgency never by itself changes Category — a smoke-detector battery Communication that begins **Stewardship** remains **Stewardship** even as deferral raises its risk and its Urgency increases under **DL-77**; Category never progresses from Stewardship to Safety merely because a Communication became more important or risky. **13. Controlled Category correction** is permitted only where the **originating responsibility** determines the immediate subject was materially misidentified, or the underlying subject materially changed. Only the originator may correct; the prior Category remains historical fact; the new Category is versioned; the reason is explainable; the Decision Trace records the correction; downstream governance affected by Category is reevaluated; completed delivery history is never rewritten; and prior decisions are never retroactively represented as having used the corrected Category. **An ordinary risk or Urgency increase is never a Category correction. 14. Category and Urgency orthogonality is reaffirmed, restating DL-77 directly, not reopened.** Neither axis contains, replaces, derives from, implies a value on, predicts, or bounds the other; no Category carries an inherent, default, minimum, or maximum Urgency. Operational Trust may consume Category as one input to an Urgency determination evaluated independently against current facts, risk, thresholds, policy, context, and audience. Valid combinations explicitly include Safety + No Interruption, Safety + Wake or Disturb, Care + No Interruption, Care + Override Protected Time, Stewardship + No Interruption, Stewardship + Wake or Disturb, Security + Interrupt Current Activity, Security + Wake or Disturb, and Experience/System/Environment + any justified Urgency. The superseded Info/Attention/Urgent ladder remains superseded. **15. No Non-Action Category.** Non-Action, No Action, Alternate Action, Suppressed, Deferred, Canceled, Expired, and Undelivered are never Categories — a governed handling outcome (alternate delivery, private redirect, changed surface or audience, Indication without content, delay, deferral, cancellation, expiration, non-delivery, reevaluation, replanning) never changes Category, which is recorded through the existing delivery, Operational Trust, and Decision Trace mechanisms. **16. Category is a downstream-input only.** It is the primary subject-classification input for disclosure, privacy, retention, re-presentation, and indication defaults, but never itself owns or executes those behaviours: **OD-49** owns retention, **OD-48** owns re-presentation, **OD-57** owns indication-versus-content, Operational Trust owns disclosure/audience/privacy/consent/appropriateness, **OD-04** owns precedence, Concierge owns delivery surface/moment/form, and **DL-77** owns Urgency — none of this decision's text sets their concrete values. **17. The canonical taxonomy is never household-configurable.** Households cannot create, delete, rename, merge, split, alias, reclassify, override as preference, or redefine a Category; Category is semantic classification, never household policy, though a household may configure Category-**driven** downstream policy under the owning decision above. **18. Category-based household policy and recommendations reuse existing mechanisms, inventing none**: HTBW-recommended defaults by Category follow the same Canonical-Recommendation/Household-Override pattern **DL-77** established; Learned Category-based policy recommendations reuse the existing **P26**/**DL-21** learning ladder (**OD-28**) exactly as **DL-75** and **DL-77** applied it to Significance and Urgency — **HTBW never learns or alters Category definitions, the enumeration, an originator's semantic assignment, the single-Category rule, or the Category/Urgency separation**; only the downstream policies that consume Category as an input may ever be learned-recommended. **19. Provenance and Explainability** reuse existing Communication, temporal-record, version-identity, Change Record, governed-reference, and Decision Trace mechanisms — no Category-specific audit log is created — and must be able to state the originating responsibility, the assigned Category, the definition version applied, the supporting immediate-purpose facts, assignment time, any correction history, and which downstream policies (disclosure, retention, re-presentation, indication, or Urgency as an input) were materially influenced. **20. Safety Category liability boundary.** Safety is a content-domain classification only. Its existence establishes no duty to monitor or warn, no guaranteed observation, classification, delivery, interruption, acknowledgment, response, action, or prevention of harm, no responsibility for safety outcomes, and no certification, code-compliance, emergency-service, medical, alarm-monitoring, or life-safety functionality — restating the existing non-negotiable **HTBW is not a life-safety system** constraint and `communication.md`'s existing Life-safety non-claim section unchanged. **21. OD-56 interaction.** This decision resolves only OD-56's Category-existence question: **yes, Safety is the seventh canonical Category.** **OD-56 is narrowed, not closed**, retaining its own disclaimer content and cross-surface survival, the authority-order.md/stewardship.md written reconciliation, safety-specific audience-bypass confirmation, dependency-missing behaviour for safety-shaped capabilities, and certified-device deference. **22. Responsibility boundaries and the second-store prohibition restate the existing pattern, creating nothing new**: Foundation (model/enumeration/definitions), the originating responsibility (assignment/correction/provenance), Operational Trust (appropriateness/Urgency, never meaning/enumeration/assignment/admissibility), Concierge (delivery, never Category), Explainability (presentation only); no Taxonomy, Categorization, Safety, Classification, Communication, or Messaging responsibility is created, and no duplicate Category registry, per-responsibility enumeration, household taxonomy, or independent audit log is introduced | [../models/communication.md](../models/communication.md), [../models/glossary.md](../models/glossary.md), [../models/operational-trust.md](../models/operational-trust.md), [../contracts/operational-trust-contract.md](../contracts/operational-trust-contract.md), [../models/decision-trace.md](../models/decision-trace.md), [../architecture/home-assistant-boundary.md](../architecture/home-assistant-boundary.md) |
| **DL-79** | **Resolves OD-56 in full. Safety is reaffirmed as DL-78's seventh Communication Category, never reopened; HTBW remains not a life-safety system; every framework responsibility expresses Safety conclusions in proportion to existing evidence-quality models, never a Safety-specific one; a one-time authenticated-Administrator acknowledgement, a certified-device deference rule, and the governed Investigation Needed outcome are accepted** (P15, P21, P24, P26, P27, P28, P29, P30, P32, DL-26, DL-27, DL-29, DL-30, DL-33, DL-34, DL-37, DL-38, DL-40, DL-41, DL-56, DL-57, DL-58, DL-63, DL-77, DL-78). **1. Safety is not reopened.** DL-78 already accepts Safety as the seventh canonical Communication Category, identifying content domain only, establishing no duty to monitor or warn and no guarantee of observation, classification, delivery, interruption, acknowledgement, response, mitigation, protection, or outcome, and no certification, code-compliance, emergency-service, medical, or alarm-monitoring functionality. **2. HTBW is not a life-safety system** remains the existing non-negotiable constitutional constraint (`authority-order.md`), unchanged and unweakened by Safety's existence as a Category. **3. Written reconciliation.** Stewardship's accepted safety-related scope of care (recognising, evaluating, and caring for safety-related conditions and obligations) and the non-negotiable life-safety constraint are not in tension: Stewardship may create or recognise a care obligation, originate a truthful governed Safety Communication, recommend household attention, and coordinate permitted responses through the existing responsibilities, while asserting no life-safety responsibility, no guaranteed detection, warning, delivery, protection, mitigation, or outcome. The canonical responsibility flow is: **Truth** owns facts at their actual scope; **Identity** owns identity assertions and their confidence at their actual scope; **Operational Trust** determines appropriateness and grants Urgency under **DL-77**; **Stewardship** owns care and obligations; **Continuity** provides legitimately retained context; **Concierge** coordinates governed help, delivery, surface, moment, and form; **Explainability** assembles the evidence and reasoning without changing ownership. A certified life-safety or protective device remains authoritative for its own domain throughout. **4. No Safety-specific fact, confidence, or evidence model is created.** Safety conclusions are expressed under the same accepted models as every other domain: **DL-58** Truth Fact Confidence (Low/Moderate/High/Very High) for evidentiary strength, **DL-38**'s Identity Fusion confidence for identity assertions, and **DL-63**'s Genuine Truth Conflict definition for disagreeing sources. Every conclusion must preserve or reference contributing facts, assertions, source, observation time, evidence quality, confidence, scope, staleness, uncertainty, disagreement, missing dependencies, and the reasoning connecting evidence to conclusion — never collapsing observed fact, identity assertion, risk evaluation, confidence conclusion, recommendation, permitted action, and delivery outcome into one statement. **5. Material uncertainty must be resident-visible**, expressed in understandable household language (for example *reported*, *likely*, *possible*, *uncertain*, *unable to determine*, *current state unavailable*, *evidence is conflicting*, *additional inspection recommended*) mapped to the existing confidence model above — never only in Decision Trace metadata reachable solely through a later Explainability request. **6. Missing, stale, conflicting, or insufficient evidence never forces or implies a conclusion.** HTBW states what is known, what is not known, why it is not known, names the unavailable, stale, or conflicting dependency, qualifies the conclusion to its actual evidence quality, and may recommend household inspection or validation — restating **DL-41** (`Unavailable` is a dependency outcome, never a trust or permission failure, and is never silently converted to a healthy or safe state) and Truth's existing `unknown`/`expired`/`stale` vocabulary, inventing nothing new. **7. Investigation Needed is accepted as a governed conclusion/handling outcome** — never a Category, an Urgency level, an alarm state, a native platform state, a guarantee, or a new responsibility. It applies where available evidence shows something deserves household attention but is insufficient to support a stronger conclusion and human observation is required; the resulting Communication states what is known, when it was observed, what remains unknown and why, whether the condition may still be active, which dependency is unavailable or conflicting, and what the household should inspect. It never automatically authorises audible delivery, repeated delivery, protected-time override, waking a resident, a broader audience, or a disclosure bypass — the message-level recommended Urgency and the **DL-77** granted Urgency remain separately governed. **8. The calm-home doctrine is preserved**: Safety architecture optimises for the household understanding what happened, what is known, what is uncertain, what deserves attention, and why the Home did or did not communicate — never for maximising alerts, alarming language, noisy or repeated delivery, exaggerated certainty, or automatic escalation. **9. A one-time authenticated-Administrator acknowledgement is required before Safety capabilities are enabled for a Home.** The acknowledgement states, in household-facing language, that HTBW is not a life-safety system; that HTBW may communicate about Safety-related conditions, observations, guidance, and obligations without guaranteeing detection, observation, classification, monitoring, Communication creation, delivery, interruption, acknowledgement, response, mitigation, protection, prevention of harm, or outcome; that certified alarms and protective systems remain authoritative; that Safety-related capabilities may become `Unavailable` under **DL-41**; that Stewardship may care for Safety-related conditions without assuming life-safety responsibility; and that Safety follows ordinary audience, privacy, consent, disclosure, Urgency, and delivery governance. **Only an authenticated, logged-in Administrator may accept**, reusing **DL-56**'s consent-record shape (actor, scope, granted/effective time, version) extended to a Home-level governance-boundary acceptance rather than person-scoped evidence consent; a native administrator flag confers the authority to accept this specific acknowledgement, exactly as it already stands for other administrator-gated changes, but — restating **DL-57** unchanged — confers no care, guardianship, or proxy authority. The acceptance record preserves or references the authenticated Administrator, the acknowledgement version, acceptance timestamp, Home/configuration scope, and the Safety capabilities enabled under it, reusing existing governed-record, version-identity, and retention mechanisms — no new acknowledgement store is created. **10. Installer and household authority remain distinct**: a vendor, installer, integrator, consultant, or configurator's technical setup action is never household governance acceptance; only the authenticated Administrator's acceptance satisfies section 9, and the record distinguishes who performed technical setup from who accepted. **11. The acceptance record must be reviewable and exportable** as a household governance record, reusing existing governed-record, Decision Trace, evidence-package, and retention mechanisms — no new evidence store is created. **12. Acknowledgement placement is a record-shape and authority requirement only; the commissioning or onboarding surface that captures it is explicitly not decided here.** The repository has no onboarding or first-run experience architecture today — a residual already named and owned by **OD-85** (#172, question 4) and carried by the product-transition review on #171 — and this decision does not invent one; when that surface is designed, it must carry the acknowledgement this section defines. **13. Reacceptance is required only for a material governance-boundary change** — an expansion of Safety capability scope, a change to the non-life-safety claims, certified-device deference, dependency-failure behaviour, household obligations, or what HTBW represents it can do — never for a bug fix, UI change, non-substantive wording cleanup, added example, refactor, or documentation clarification. **14. Safety creates no Safety-specific audience, disclosure, or recipient model.** It follows the same audience, privacy, consent, and disclosure governance as every Category (**DL-34**, **P32** — delivery degrades, never the governance) and the same existing caretaker, custody, and delegated-access relationships already accepted (**DL-49** Custody Period, **DL-57** Delegated Access Grant, Foundation `caretaker-of`) for people, pets, assets, and spaces — no new guardian, caretaker, dependent, or recipient model is created, and no gap in that existing coverage was found. **15. Message-level recommended Urgency is accepted as an ordinary application of DL-77**, never a Safety-specific Urgency model: a governed Communication definition or scenario may carry an HTBW-recommended Urgency (for example, an active certified smoke-alarm report recommending Wake or Disturb, or a Safety planning reminder recommending No Interruption) exactly as **DL-77**'s Canonical HTBW Recommendation already provides for every Category; the message-level recommendation is never the final granted entitlement, which Operational Trust alone determines under **DL-77**. **16. Safety bypasses no governance** — not Truth, Identity, Operational Trust, Stewardship, Continuity, Concierge, Explainability, audience, privacy, consent, disclosure, Urgency, delivery, caretaker authority, dependency governance, or native-state authority; Safety is a Category, never a constitutional exception. **17. Missing dependency means Unavailable, restating DL-41 unchanged**: a missing, failed, stale-beyond-validity, or disconnected dependency makes a Safety-shaped capability `Unavailable`, with the missing dependency named in a sentence the household can act on; `Unavailable` is an acceptable, more trustworthy architectural outcome than false confidence, and is never silently converted to healthy, safe, inactive, or monitored. **18. Certified-device deference.** A certified life-safety or protective device remains authoritative for its own domain. HTBW may communicate that the device reported a condition; HTBW must never reinterpret, restate as stronger, expand, certify, or replace that claim, and must never suppress, delay, or defer the native alarm. Permitted: *"The kitchen smoke alarm reported an alarm condition at 2:11 AM."* Forbidden without independent stronger evidence: *"There is a fire in the kitchen."* **19. HTBW-derived Safety observations remain evidence-bounded**, characterising the source correctly, preserving evidence quality and confidence, stating actual scope, exposing material uncertainty, and distinguishing observation from conclusion from recommendation from permitted action — *"the sensor under the sink reported wet"* is never *"the house is flooding"*; *"the camera classified the animal as a possible cougar"* is never *"a cougar is threatening the household"* absent evidence supporting that stronger claim. **20. Temporal provenance and delay-relevance disclosure reuse the existing temporal-record and Decision Trace architecture (P29, P30), inventing no new mechanism**: observation time, authoritative-report time, source timestamp, Communication creation time, most recent reevaluation time, delivery-attempt time, successful-delivery time, and acknowledgement/cancellation/expiration/resolution time where applicable remain distinct and preserved; where delay materially affects relevance, resident-facing delivery states the observation time or elapsed age in understandable language, and an old observation is never presented as current without qualification. **21. Complete Safety lifecycle Explainability reuses the existing Decision Trace, Truth, Identity, Stewardship, Continuity, and delivery-record architecture** to reconstruct what fact was observed, at what scope, when, from which source, the source's authority class (certified, native, externally authoritative, HTBW-derived, or inferred) and availability, the evidence quality and confidence applied, what remained unknown, which dependencies were unavailable or conflicting, the conclusion reached, why the Communication was categorised Safety, the message-level recommended and DL-77-granted Urgency, the audience and disclosure decisions, the delivery decision and its timing, and the exact claim made versus the stronger claim not made — no independent Safety audit trail is created. **22. The framework-wide evidence chain is named, not newly decided**: Truth contributes facts; Identity contributes assertions and confidence; Operational Trust evaluates appropriateness from available facts, assertions, context, and policy; Stewardship contributes obligations and significance; Continuity contributes legitimately retained context; Concierge assembles governed delivery; Explainability reconstructs what happened and why — this is the union of already-accepted **P15, P27, P28, DL-26, DL-27, DL-30, DL-38, DL-58**, named here as a cross-cutting doctrine applying to every responsibility and every domain, Safety included, and requiring no new responsibility or separately governed decision. **23. No new responsibility, store, or canonical term is created** beyond Investigation Needed itself (section 7) — no Safety, Monitoring, Emergency, Investigation, Evidence Quality, Acknowledgement, or Caretaker responsibility; no duplicate native-state store, Safety history store, Safety audit log, separate evidence store, new acknowledgement database, embedded delivery-history array, parallel caretaker registry, parallel confidence model, or Safety-specific source-of-truth mechanism | [../governance/authority-order.md](../governance/authority-order.md), [../models/communication.md](../models/communication.md), [../models/stewardship.md](../models/stewardship.md), [../models/operational-trust.md](../models/operational-trust.md), [../models/decision-trace.md](../models/decision-trace.md), [../architecture/home-assistant-boundary.md](../architecture/home-assistant-boundary.md), [../scenarios/stewardship-use-cases.md](../scenarios/stewardship-use-cases.md) |

| **DL-90** | **Decoupled Voice Interaction Capability Model.** Accepted 2026-10-26 (Issue #198, formal acceptance review PASS). Distinguishes **Capability** (what a device can technically do), **Participation** (whether it is explicitly selected to take part in a Room), and **Interaction Function Assignment** (which specific experience-endpoint function — `voice_input`, `spoken_response_output`, `music`, `video`, `announcement`, `conversation` — a participating capability is assigned to fulfill), deliberately not reusing **Role** (the glossary's existing person-authority class). **`voice_input`** represents the configured device(s) used to hear voice interactions in a Room; **`spoken_response_output`** (replacing the generic "audio_output" term used in **DL-88**'s own still-pending draft, to avoid colliding with music/media `audio_output` semantics) represents the Room's configured destination for Concierge's own spoken responses, consumed by and not altering the existing Response Delivery Space ([concierge-contract.md](../contracts/concierge-contract.md) §6). A device possessing both capabilities does not imply both assignments — an integrated voice-assistant device may be assigned `voice_input` only, both, or (with a separately assigned `spoken_response_output` elsewhere) neither alone. **No cardinality assumption** (exactly one device per role) is made; the model must remain able to represent multiple microphones, output groups, or future redundancy, exactly as Room Configuration already does for multiple participating music speakers. **Merged Rooms are reconciled, not reopened** (**DL-67**, **DL-68**): a microphone detecting an interaction provides originating-space evidence only; it does not automatically establish the final Interaction Space, which Concierge continues to resolve using Foundation configuration and Truth evidence exactly as today. **Voice input is evidence, never authority**: a microphone or satellite does not by itself establish person identity, authority, intent, presence truth, or final Room context — restating **DL-06**'s existing Identity Evidence/Identity Assertion/Contextual Person-Presence Fact separation for the voice-interaction case. Extends, without replacing, Room Configuration's existing "voice assistant context" ([room-configuration-contract.md](../contracts/room-configuration-contract.md), [room-configuration.md](../models/room-configuration.md)); an integrated voice assistant continues to resolve identically to today | A device's capability treated as an automatic role assignment; the capturing device assumed to be the responding device; a microphone treated as establishing identity, presence, or Room context by itself; exactly-one-device-per-role assumed; **DL-67**/**DL-68** or Room Configuration's existing voice-assistant resolution order reopened | [adr-decoupled-voice-interaction-capability-architecture.md](../architecture/adr-decoupled-voice-interaction-capability-architecture.md) |

unchanged. **Continuity is preserved**: a performance optimization must not route a context-dependent follow-up into a fast deterministic path where doing so would lose conversational context required to interpret the request correctly. **Existing governed Concierge audio-delivery behavior is reused, not duplicated**: room speaker selection, Sonos selection, duck/pause, TTS delivery, and resume existing "must not announce merely because it was permitted to act" prohibition (**P32**), not a new prohibition. **Graceful degradation is explicit and reuses existing contracts** for Home Intelligence unavailability, Voice Identity unavailability, `spoken_response_output` unavailability (does not prevent an otherwise-permitted action), and a failed `voice_input` device (does not affect unrelated interaction surfaces) — no new fallback mechanism is invented. **Privacy stages are explicitly distinguished** (listening availability, wake-word processing, active capture, speech recognition, identity processing, storage/retention), restating the existing "no wake-word decision" finding, **DL-50**'s "speaker evidence never gates transcription" rule (D6), and the existing zero-default raw-voice retention rule ([privacy.md](../architecture/privacy.md)) — extended, not newly created, to ordinary (non-enrollment) voice-interaction capture. **A measurable, non-SLA performance-metrics vocabulary** (wake-word-to-listening, utterance-to-recognition, recognition-to-action, action-to-state-change, utterance-to-first-response, interaction-to-outcome, and related **DL-86**/**DL-41**, or the no-wake-word finding reopened | [adr-decoupled-voice-interaction-capability-architecture.md](../architecture/adr-decoupled-voice-interaction-capability-architecture.md) |
| **DL-92** | **Accepted 2026-10-27 (Issue #76, formal acceptance review PASS, following bounded reference and terminology corrections).** **Governed-Record Persistence Mechanism.** The Home Assistant Storage helper (`Store`), scoped one file (or bounded set) per owning responsibility, is the authoritative, default persistence mechanism for all three record kinds **Current Projection, Change Record, and Snapshot** — verified durable (versioned JSON, debounced/atomic writes, documented corruption recovery, migration via `_async_migrate_func`), backup-covered, and never presented to a resident as removable configuration the way a config entry is (**#146** item 1). **Connected Storage is never required for baseline operation**; it is available strictly as the already-accepted **External History Retention** extension (**DL-42**) a responsibility may configure for a Change Record class it wants to retain longer than is practical natively — never a parallel authority, and never for Current Projections, which remain native always. **Decision Trace's own persistence surface is not decided here** and remains **OD-29**'s (#79) question, whose own stated options include the Home Assistant Logbook, Connected Storage, or both. **Config-entry removal is distinguished from governed-record deletion**: removing or reinstalling the HTBW integration's config entry does not, by itself, delete or recreate governed records, because native removal of a Store-backed file is source-level only, never an automatic or documented resident-facing side effect of config-entry removal; **a count-based ring buffer is explicitly rejected as a conforming retention mechanism** because it cannot honor a Preservation Hold. **No second Recorder is created**: this decision persists only the governed meaning Home Assistant does not already represent (**DL-46**), never a copy of native Recorder/Logbook/statistics data. **Migration preserves canonical identity**: a storage key, file path, or row position is never a record's canonical identity absent a future **OD-38** decision; a future mechanism change must not silently rewrite historical meaning. **Retention duration values (OD-05, OD-26, OD-49), Preservation Hold governance (OD-39), deletion-versus-preservation reconciliation (OD-36), and the identifier/correlation scheme (OD-38) are not decided here and remain separately owned** | A central History or Memory responsibility invented; | **DL-93** | **Accepted 2026-10-27 (Issue #132, formal acceptance review PASS, following bounded stale-reference corrections).** **Reasoning Provider Strategy.** HTBW permits, and selects none of, three household postures: a **local/self-hosted** Reasoning provider, a **household-approved external/cloud** Reasoning provider, or **no Reasoning provider configured** — the last a fully legitimate posture under **DL-41**, never a degraded state. **Local residency is never automatically trustworthy; otherwise the household's designated Guest fallback Person Extension (**DL-71**), a real, deliberately-configured Person whose settings are consulted without any Identity Assertion binding; otherwise the **DL-33** unidentified-person policy. **No Room involvement, no numeric identity-likelihood threshold, and no second anonymous-person type is created.** **Configuration is Integration- and Person-scoped only** — there is no Room scope for Reasoning or Home Steward authorization or provider assignment; YES authorizes resolution. **Configured fallback, never discovery**: Person-specific provider → Integration default → unavailable; a terminal authorization denial never enters the fallback chain, and provider unavailability never enters as a trust or permission outcome (**DL-41**). **Reasoning and Home Steward are independent**: denial of one never affects the other, and neither is a fallback for the other. **Reasoning may reason, never govern**: permitted purposes are general knowledge Q&A, wording/presentation, summarisation, natural-language interpretation, and authorized-context reasoning; Operational Trust, never the provider, determines disclosure scope (**DL-34**); configuration-time disclosure states residency, purpose, fallback role, and the effect of non-configuration, without requiring repetitive per-interaction announcement. **Explainability reuses the existing Decision Trace structure**: effective Person used, capability requested, authorization result, provider identity/scope, fallback path, purpose, and residency are ordinary trace content, not a new record class; | **DL-94** | **Accepted 2026-10-27 (Issue #102, formal acceptance review PASS).** **Indication, Room-Delivery Audience Preference, and Message-Scoped Room-Delivery Authorization.** Resolves **OD-57** in full. **Three delivery forms, formally distinct and never merged:** (1) **Indication** — content-free, asserting only that something is outstanding, disclosing no recipient identity, subject, content, relationship, sensitive content class, or concealed-resource existence (**DL-72**, unchanged); (2) **Room-Delivery Authorization Challenge** — a bounded, named extension of **DL-37**'s neutral-challenge class, permitted to disclose exactly that a private Communication exists, its canonical **Urgency** level, that private delivery has not completed, that the current Room audience falls outside the intended Person's standing delivery permission, and a request for this-Communication-only Room-delivery authorization — and nothing else; (b) which known, co-present audiences — Household, specifically selected individual Household members, and Guest, each independently permitted or not, reusing **DL-71**'s relationship-based-recipient and multiple-recipient evaluation model — satisfy standing permission without a one-message exception. **A Person present with another Person is not thereby an unauthorized audience**; the Preference, not mere co-presence, determines sufficiency. Operational Trust evaluates whether the Preference is currently permitted and safe exactly as it already does for the Audience-Uncertainty Routing Preference; the Preference itself grants nothing. **Message-Scoped Room-Delivery Authorization** (new, narrow, OD-57-owned record, never a second retry/escalation/acknowledgement engine): when standing audience permission is insufficient and a Challenge is issued, the Communication carries exactly one authorization state — **Pending**, **Authorized**, or **Denied** — scoped to that Communication alone. **Explicit Yes** (from the sufficiently resolved intended Person alone, at the existing required Identity/evidence level; no other Household member or Guest may authorize another Person's Communication) authorizes Room delivery of that Communication only and changes no Person Configuration, Category, Urgency, or future Communication. **Explicit No** denies the Room path for that Communication only, clears the Pending state, triggers no repeat request for that Communication, and never marks the Communication delivered, refused, cancelled, or acknowledged; Guest (**DL-33**, **DL-71**) remains the distinct trust-and-permissions construct applied once a co-present participant is actually resolved as a non-resident. | **DL-95** | **Accepted 2026-10-28 (Issue #114, formal acceptance review PASS, following the bounded Scenario 15 terminology correction already made in commit `a94905b` during Phase 1 recovery; no further remediation required).** **Communication Lifecycle and Delivery Attempt Outcome Model.** Resolves **OD-44** in full. **Two levels, never flattened:** (1) **Communication lifecycle** — exactly one current state at a time: **Created** (exists and is outstanding, from origination, independent of any Delivery Attempt), **Suppressed** (withheld by an Operational-Trust-governed decision; always produces a Decision Trace as an Intentional Non-Action), **Acknowledged** (an identified Person's explicit act; never inferred from presentation or silence), **Expired** (its relevance window closed without a terminal outcome, against a referenced governing policy), **Superseded** (replaced by a later Communication via an explicit Governed Reference), **Resolved by origin** (the originator withdrew it because the underlying condition cleared; the resident may never have seen it), and **Undeliverable** (no currently permitted surface could convey it at all; terminal; must be reported, never silent). (2) **Delivery Attempt outcome** — **Attempted** / **Delivered** / **Presented** / **Failed**, each bounded to one delivery act on one surface and preserved as immutable history (**DL-26**); a Communication may have many Delivery Attempts; a failed attempt never makes the Communication itself "failed," and a later successful attempt never erases an earlier failed one. **Presentation Outcome is consumed unchanged from DL-54** (**Presented** / **Failed** / **Unknown** / **Attestation Unavailable**, evaluated by modality and evidence) as the sub-determination of a `Delivered` attempt; this decision does not redefine or duplicate it, and `Unknown`/`Attestation Unavailable` never decay into "not presented." **DL-94 is consumed unchanged**: Indication and the Room-Delivery Authorization Challenge are each themselves Communications — independently originated, audience-evaluated, and delivered under this same two-level model, each producing their own Delivery Attempt and Presentation Outcome records — never a delivery of the underlying protected Communication's content; Explicit Yes/No/No Response are Message-Scoped Room-Delivery Authorization states, never delivery, refusal, cancellation, resolution-by-origin, or acknowledgement of the underlying Communication, which continues independently (private delivery proceeds regardless of the Room-path outcome). **Suppressed and Undeliverable are governed non-actions, satisfying DL-46**, without ever fabricating a Delivery Attempt that did not occur: Suppressed records a deliberate decision not to attempt a specific delivery while other paths may remain available and the Communication remains active; Undeliverable records that no permitted path remains at all. **Completed remains superseded and does not reappear**: `Resolved by origin` and `Acknowledged` replace it and are never collapsed with each other, with Stewardship obligation Completion (**DL-71**), or with acknowledgement-validity criteria. **Boundaries preserved, nothing absorbed**: acknowledgement validity and acknowledger-identification criteria remain **OD-45**'s; retry intervals, cadence, and abandonment remain **OD-54**'s; escalation remains **OD-22**'s — each is supplied only the truthful Delivered/Failed/Unknown/Acknowledged facts this decision already establishes. **The architecture was already substantively present** in this ADR, `communication.md`, and `concierge-contract.md` prior to this review; this decision formalizes its governance status and corrects one documentation contradiction found during review (Scenario 15's terminal-state label, commit `a94905b`) | Flattening the two levels into one enumeration; | **DL-96** | **Accepted 2026-10-28 (Issue #115, formal acceptance review PASS, following two bounded substantive refinements identified during independent review and incorporated below — a dismissal-explicitness qualifier and a multi-recipient-acknowledgement rule — neither requiring new Owner policy; no further remediation required).** **Acknowledgement Semantics.** Resolves **OD-45** in full. **Acknowledgement is an explicit, Communication-specific responsive act** — closing, dismissing, confirming, denying, or answering — by a Person Identity resolves to a `known` assertion meeting whatever Required Identity Band Operational Trust configures for this operation (**DL-36**, **DL-39** consumed unchanged; no new identity confidence scale is created), who is also within the Communication's resolved Intended Audience (**DL-71**). A **DL-37** Confirmation answer and a **DL-94** Explicit Yes/No/No Response are never themselves Acknowledgement of an unrelated or underlying protected Communication; where one responsive act legitimately satisfies two independent bounded questions, both are independently justified and separately recorded. Ignoring a Home Assistant Repairs issue remains not a Person-attributed acknowledgement. **Boundaries preserved, nothing absorbed**: escalation-consumption policy remains **OD-22**'s; retry interval, cadence, and give-up policy remain **OD-54**'s — each supplied only the truthful Acknowledged/unknown facts this decision establishes. **The architecture was already substantially distributed** across DL-36, DL-37, DL-39, DL-40, DL-54, DL-55, DL-57, DL-71, DL-95, and the existing glossary definition prior to this review; this decision reconciles and formalizes it, correcting the dismissal-sufficiency and multi-recipient gaps Phase 1's recovery had not yet resolved | A new identity confidence scale created for acknowledgement; a bare dismiss/clear event credited as Acknowledgement without establishing genuine responsiveness; Confirmation or DL-94 authorization treated as Acknowledgement; Acknowledgement treated as Care Evidence or Stewardship Completion; unacknowledged delivery converted into failure; a per-recipient acknowledgement sub-model invented where none is required; Stewardship delegation (DL-57) treated as extending to Communication acknowledgement; retry or escalation policy decided here | [adr-resident-communication-and-delivery-separation.md](../architecture/adr-resident-communication-and-delivery-separation.md), [../models/communication.md](../models/communication.md), [../contracts/concierge-contract.md](../contracts/concierge-contract.md), [../models/stewardship.md](../models/stewardship.md) |

| **DL-97** | **Accepted 2026-10-28 (Issue #108, formal acceptance review PASS, incorporating the Owner Policy Response recorded on #108 — no HTBW-wide default grace-period value — and three bounded substantive refinements identified during independent review: a new-specification-versus-re-resolution test, a no-self-authorizing-trigger rule, and an explicit notified-is-not-accountable statement; none requiring further new Owner policy; no further remediation required).** **Escalation Ladder Semantics and Defaults.** Resolves **OD-22** in full, consuming **OD-50**'s prior resolution into it. **Confirms, does not reopen, the constitutional boundary**: there is one escalation architecture, serving obligations and Communications identically; Stewardship owns the ladder and escalation intent; Operational Trust owns authority; Concierge executes; no Escalation responsibility exists; no second ladder may be created (**authority-order.md**). **Escalation is a governed change of who is accountable, expressed as a new recorded Intended Audience Specification** — reusing **DL-71**'s existing five accepted forms (Named Person, Role/Authority Class, Relationship-based, Anyone Present With Authority, Household) as the ladder's rungs; no sixth form or separate rung vocabulary is created. "Household authority" and "external service provider" are not new constructs — both are the **Role/Authority Class** form, naming whatever Role the household configures (ordinarily an owner/administrator-equivalent Role, or `service provider` for a non-resident participant holding a **DL-57** minimal Person record). **Re-resolution of an unchanged specification is not escalation**: a dynamic form's existing per-attempt re-evaluation (**DL-71**) resolving to a different currently-eligible Person under the *same* specification remains ordinary delivery or retry, never escalation; delivery to the new party is the resulting mechanism, never the cause. **No HTBW-wide default grace-period or elapsed-time value exists** (Owner Policy Response, #108): escalation timing is household-configured, via Integration Configuration, as part of each obligation's or Communication class's existing **Escalation intent** field (`stewardship.md`); absent configuration, elapsed time alone never makes a rung eligible; independently configured evidence-based triggers remain available under their own accepted rules regardless. **Stop conditions**: obligation condition `met`/`waived` (**DL-48**) stops escalation for that obligation; Communication acknowledgement (**DL-96**) may stop that Communication's escalation per configured policy without resolving the obligation condition (**DL-71**'s three-distinct-concepts rule unchanged); deferral (**DL-48**) never erases condition truth; disclosure denial at a prospective rung means that rung is never executed. **Top-of-ladder**: no universal guaranteed terminal rung and no emergency/external-authority behaviour is invented (life-safety non-claim, `authority-order.md`); an unresolvable audience at any point, including a configured fallback Role resolving to nobody, is an accountability gap (**DL-71**), reported, never fabricated or silently broadened. **Pattern reporting is distinct from a rung advance** (Scenario 7): a repeated-unmet pattern is its own newly reportable concern, Concierge changing approach rather than repeating an identical reminder, orthogonal to any accountability change. **Scenarios 5 and 7 reproduce exactly** under this model. **Boundaries preserved, nothing absorbed**: **OD-04** precedence, **OD-54** retry interval/cadence/give-up, and **DL-57**/**DL-71**/**DL-75**/**DL-76**/**DL-96** are each consumed unchanged and none is redefined | A second escalation ladder or Escalation responsibility; emergency-calling or external-authority behaviour invented at the top of the ladder; pattern reporting treated as merely another rung; Significance or Action-Risk Classification treated as a second escalation architecture; retry called escalation | [../models/stewardship.md](../models/stewardship.md), [../contracts/stewardship-contract.md](../contracts/stewardship-contract.md), [../models/communication.md](../models/communication.md), [../contracts/concierge-contract.md](../contracts/concierge-contract.md), [../models/glossary.md](../models/glossary.md) |

| **DL-98** | **Accepted 2026-10-28 (Issue #120, formal acceptance review PASS, incorporating the Owner Policy Response recorded on #120 — no HTBW-wide default retry count or interval — and refinements identified during independent review: an explicit three-mechanism distinction separating DL-54's single-failure fallback, Delivery Retry proper, and OD-48's re-presentation; (2) **Delivery Retry proper** — a household-configured, scheduled/recurring policy (attempt count and interval) Concierge consumes **in addition to**, never instead of, DL-54's fallback; (3) **Re-presentation (OD-48, unchanged, still open)** — triggered by a Person's room transition, categorically unrelated to any delivery outcome. **No HTBW-wide default retry count or interval exists** (Owner Policy Response, #120): retry count and interval are household choices, configured during Integration setup, optionally keyed by the Communication's already-governed Urgency (**DL-77**) — never a new priority, significance, or Urgency scale, and never a basis for Operational Trust to reevaluate the granted entitlement; the Communication remains outstanding" is itself a distinct, honestly representable condition**, never collapsed into any of DL-95's seven states; DL-54's fallback and DL-97's Stewardship escalation/pattern-reporting each remain independently available regardless. **Delivery Retry is repeating delivery under the same, already-resolved Intended Audience Specification** — never requiring the same physical surface or modality; a dynamic specification's own per-attempt re-resolution (**DL-71**) to a different currently-eligible Person is distinct from retry, answering only "who is this for, right now," never itself a retry or escalation event; only a Stewardship-recorded new specification is escalation (**DL-97**, unchanged). **Every attempt receives independent, current-context Operational Trust evaluation**, exactly as DL-54 already requires; a prior private-surface authorization is never reused to authorize a later shared-surface attempt; Room progression remains governed by **DL-94** unchanged, with an Explicit No permanent for that Communication's Room path, never re-asked under the guise of retry. **Stop conditions, precisely distinguished**: `Delivered` and `Acknowledged` (**DL-96**) each stop retry (purpose satisfied); | **DL-99** | **Accepted 2026-10-28 (Issue #117, formal acceptance review PASS, following one genuine Owner Policy Question identified and resolved during the review itself — see below — no further remediation required).** **Communication Re-Presentation Policy.** Resolves **OD-48** in full. **A Communication has no location** and is never duplicated, moved, or transferred; where a Person moves and a Communication remains outstanding, Concierge may make a **new Delivery Attempt** on a newly appropriate surface — *Follow-Me Communication* remains superseded terminology (Part 3, this document). **Ownership is a three-way split, inventing no new authority**: Continuity holds the preference; Operational Trust (**P32**) determines whether re-presentation is currently permitted; Concierge decides whether, where, and how to attempt it — identical in shape to the existing Room-Delivery Audience Preference (**DL-94**) and Ordinary Delivery/Audience-Uncertainty Routing Preference (**DL-72**) pattern it sits beside. **The trigger is a Room transition Fact** (Truth-owned), reused unchanged from Follow-Me media's own "unambiguous room transition — origin and destination both known and different" requirement; a missed or ambiguous transition is never retroactively invented. An explicit resident request ("read that here") is **Retrieval**, a separate, already-governed mechanism, never re-presentation. **The preference is Person-scoped and strictly opt-in** — reaffirming `continuity-contract.md`'s existing rule that **a missing preference is never silently replaced by a platform default**: absence of configuration is reported as an unmet precondition, never a fabricated enabled/disabled value. The preference may optionally be refined by Category (**DL-78**, which names OD-48 explicitly among its downstream consumers) and/or Urgency (**DL-77**), consumed unchanged — no new classification axis is created. **Owner Policy Response incorporated (Issue #117)**: re-presentation is opt-in and Person-scoped; where enabled, the household configures the permitted repetition behaviour — any repetition limit and/or cooldown — during Integration setup; **no HTBW-wide default numeric repetition count or cooldown exists**. Where re-presentation is enabled but no repetition policy is configured, this is **never** interpreted as license to re-present on every qualifying Room transition indefinitely — the Communication remains outstanding and eligible under its existing lifecycle, but repetition itself stays bounded by explicit household configuration, directly mirroring **DL-98**'s own "no retry loop begins absent configuration" shape; this is never a basis to fabricate `Undeliverable` or any other lifecycle state. **Stop conditions**: `Acknowledged` (**DL-96**), `Resolved by origin`/`Expired`/`Superseded` (**DL-95**), and `Undeliverable` each end further re-presentation — directly confirmed, for the acknowledged case, by `continuity-use-cases.md` Use Case 2 Acceptance Scenario 2.3 ("Tom acknowledges → re-presentation stops; a household may still configure which existing Operational Trust mode (Explicit/Assisted/Autonomous) resolves a genuine conflict, not whether contention exists. **Provider and Home Assistant mechanics remain untouched** (**P21**, **DL-46**): no play/pause/resume/join/group/queue/handoff behavior is decided here. | **DL-103** | **Accepted 2026-10-28 (Issue #137, formal acceptance review PASS, following one genuine Owner Policy Question asked and answered during this formal acceptance review itself, resolving a self-authored reason-taxonomy overreach identified during independent review — the proposed `not_suitable`/`household_choice` pairing had an undecidable boundary even for its own canonical example, and `household_choice` was tautological, restating a fact the Deliberately Excluded Participation state already establishes; | **DL-104** | **Accepted 2026-10-28 (Issue #84, formal acceptance review PASS, following one bounded substantive refinement identified and resolved during this review itself — Phase 1's self-derived "monotonic per-Subject revision counter" did not hold up to independent challenge, since nothing in accepted architecture establishes that a revision sequence is never reused or that restore/migration correctly reconstructs the last number used; replaced with an opaque per-version identifier, with ordering supplied unchanged by the already-required Prior/New Version Reference chain and Effective/Recorded Time — and one additional precision drawn directly from already-accepted text — a one-shot immutable record (Domain Event, Snapshot, Decision Trace) collapses Object Identity and Version Identity into a single immutable Record Identity, rather than receiving a Subject Type/Subject ID/Version triple it has no continuously-revised Subject to justify; neither requiring new Owner policy; no further remediation required).** **Identifier, Version Identity, Correlation, and Causation Strategy.** Resolves **OD-38** in full. **OD-01 independently re-verified as closed and non-blocking** (**DL-31**/**DL-92**); **DL-92** itself already defers identity to this decision and imposes exactly one constraint — identity is record data, never a storage key, file path, row position, array index, or transient runtime address — satisfied unchanged. **Two identity shapes, never one forced pattern**: a record with a continuously-revised Subject (Room Configuration, Person Configuration, Policy, an obligation, a Communication, a session) already carries, as constitutional Change Record fields, **Subject Type** + **Subject ID** (**Governed Object Identity**, stable across every revision) and **Prior/New Version Reference** (**Version Identity**, naming exactly one revision) — two distinct concepts, confirmed directly from `temporal-record.md`'s own required-fields list, never newly synthesized. A one-shot immutable occurrence with no continuously-revised Subject behind it — a **Domain Event**, a **Snapshot**, a **Decision Trace** — instead carries a single immutable **Record Identity**, collapsing object and version identity into one value; a Decision Trace's own Record Identity is its **Trace ID**. **Version Identity is an opaque, per-version identifier**, never a monotonic counter (its "never reused" and "correctly reconstructed across restore" properties are not established by any accepted architecture and impose a restore/migration correctness burden an opaque token does not share), never a content hash (its sole motivation — avoiding full-payload comparison — is already met by the constitutionally required **Changed Fields** element; it would otherwise require inventing an undecided canonicalization standard for no further capability), and never a bare timestamp (clock skew can make a later-recorded version carry an earlier timestamp, unacceptable for an exact identity; Effective/Recorded Time remain separately required for their own bitemporal purpose, unconflated with identity). Ordering is supplied, unchanged, by the existing Prior/New Version Reference chain and Effective/Recorded Time — no field does double duty. **Complete exact-version reference (Governed Reference)**: `{Subject Type, Subject ID, Version Identity}` for a revised Subject; `{Record Class, Record Identity}` alone for a one-shot record — both resolve exactly and unambiguously across responsibilities without a central allocator, consistent with "each responsibility owns Version Identity for its own records." **Correlation Identity is a derived property of the Governed Reference graph, never a separately-generated token**: every record cites the reference of whatever triggered it; for the ordinary one-trigger/one-evaluation case a Decision Trace's own Trace ID already anchors everything it cites; where one trigger produces several independent traces, each cites the shared triggering record's own reference, which is what correlates them — never a flat ID copied across unrelated traces. **Correlation lifetime is bounded to one governed-evaluation chain**, reconstructed transitively by following references; a later retry, escalation, acknowledgement, or independent evaluation is its own new evaluation with its own new identity, correlating back through the same mechanism, never silently reusing or extending a prior evaluation's identity, and no session-like construct is created. **Causation is explicit and directed, never inferred from correlation, shared Context, or timing**: within one trace it is already carried by the trace's own owned, ordered fields (trigger → Facts → Identity Assertion → capability availability → Operational Trust evaluation → decision → action/non-action → outcome); across traces, the downstream record cites the exact Governed Reference or Record Identity of what triggered it — no generic causal-graph infrastructure is created. **Home Assistant Context is native supporting evidence only** — never HTBW's Version Identity, Object Identity, Record Identity, Correlation Identity, or Decision Trace, and never proof of causation beyond the documented relationship the platform itself supplies; independently re-verified against three official Home Assistant primary sources (`contributors.home-assistant.io/data/reference/data-model/`; the `home-assistant/data.home-assistant` GitHub documentation repository's `docs/data_context.md`; `home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/state_object/`), confirming exactly three public `Context` fields (`id`, `user_id`, `parent_id`), that an automation always creates its own context with `parent_id` pointing to its trigger's context ("the context that caused this one"), and that **not every trigger creates a context** — ruling out Context as the sole correlation mechanism by proven fact, not preference; this is consistent with, and formalizes without redefining, **DL-73**'s existing "same-context sibling execution event" / "`context_user_id` match" Known Source evidence tier. a deleted or never-retained record is answered **unavailable**, never reconstructed or treated as adverse inference; existing records keep their own governing retention class; a Preservation Hold, where validly placed under **OD-39**'s own governance, protects only records that still exist and can never resurrect a deleted one or itself authorize retrospective Person Association. **OD-35, OD-36, and OD-39 remain open, independently re-verified, and are not decided or pre-empted here.** **Household incident review and an external legal request are both access/disclosure paths only, kept symmetric, never a derivation path**: each may be separately authorized to access, preserve, or disclose already-existing records exactly as each record's own governance permits; where the two disagree, the label was wrong. **No general configuration lifecycle is created.** The proposed Configure/Validate/Operate/Reconfigure/Replace/Retire sequence dissolves entirely into already-accepted mechanisms: Configure and Reconfigure are ordinary Change Records under Room Configuration's existing history model;
