Competing residents** (re-grounded, not borrowed from DL-100, refinement 1 above): each resident's own evidence remains independently eligible as that resident's own Person-scoped evidence; **no averaging, no majority rule, no silent merge into one household preference is ever created**. This follows directly from the architecture's own two-scope structure without needing DL-100 at all: an inherently **Person-scoped** value (artist/genre/album/playlist) never actually conflicts between residents, because each Person's own preference is independently stored and independently read back only when that Person is identified — there is no shared slot to contend for. An inherently **Room-scoped** value (last song/genre, volume) is operational/historical state, not a "preference" a resident could win or lose — Room-scoped Continuity values were never designed to encode anyone's taste, so there is nothing to average. **A value whose scope assignment is itself undecided is not resolved by this decision** (for example, a lamp level — **OD-78**'s own body states this is "currently ambiguous between at least four" value classes); OD-65 states only that the eligibility rules above apply identically regardless of which scope OD-78 eventually assigns, and does not pre-assign one. **The one genuine residual this decision explicitly declines to invent**: real-time application precedence when two residents, each already holding an accepted Person-scoped preference, are simultaneously present and a shared Room-scoped operational dimension must pick one outcome right now — **DL-100 itself explicitly excludes this case** ("Room-scoped remembered experience… remains Continuity's, unaffected" by DL-100's own decorative-precedence rule), so no accepted authority currently supplies this fallback; it is a presentation/precedence question (most likely **OD-04**'s eventual policy-precedence decision, or a future extension of DL-100), never an evidence-eligibility question, and is explicitly **out of this decision's scope** — not decided, not blocked, not invented here. A **household-level learning-generated proposal** (asking the household to pick one shared Room default from conflicting resident evidence) is **not fabricated by this decision**: no "Room-scoped learned preference" record class exists to target such a proposal, and none is created. **Household Declaration/an already-accepted decision always outranks an inferred Pattern**, unconditionally. **9. Dismissal**, composing three already-accepted patterns rather than inventing a fourth: Use Case 7's own text ("the offer is repeatedly dismissed → the pattern is itself reportable," never "keep offering unchanged and unrecorded"); `communication.md`'s existing rule that a bare dismiss/clear is "acknowledgement-adjacent evidence only — never itself sufficient" absent an identified, genuinely responsive act; and **DL-37/DL-56's identical, twice-already-accepted "denial/silence is never promoted" principle**, reused a third time. A dismissal is **recorded** (an OD-28 lifecycle fact, feeding its own "does rejection suppress re-proposal" question) and **repeated dismissal is itself reportable as a Pattern about the proposal's own treatment** — but this reportable Pattern states only *"this proposal has repeatedly been dismissed,"* **never** *"the resident dislikes outcome X"* — a dismissal is never eligible as negative-weighted evidence adjusting any other Pattern's confidence, any Fusion Policy value, or any other learning computation. **Bare dismissal and explicit rejection are formally distinct**: only an identified person's genuine responsive "no" is a first-class OD-28 `rejected` lifecycle state; a bare clear, postponement, or silence-until-expiry each remain non-advancing, re-offerable, and are never promoted to "rejected" or to negative evidence. **Silence is neither acceptance nor rejection nor preference evidence** (DL-37/DL-56, restated). **10. Tradition** (Use Case 12, restated, not reopened): a repeated household occurrence may become a Pattern; it never becomes tradition, household meaning, significance, obligation, or preferred ritual without passing through the **ordinary P26/DL-21 acceptance step** — the same Suggestion→Acceptance gate every other learned behaviour passes through, never a separate "Household Declaration" mechanism (that capitalized term remains **DL-75**'s Stewardship-Significance-specific Derivation Source value and is not reused here). **11. Reasoning-provider-derived attributes**: **DL-93**/OD-67's boundary is reused unchanged — a source-supplied attribute (e.g., Music Assistant's own genre metadata) is ordinary source data; a reasoning-derived attribute (e.g., an LLM-inferred genre) is an inference that must carry explicit derived status, provider provenance, source inputs, and temporal context, and never silently becomes a Fact or a preference; where a maintained integration already supplies an attribute as source metadata, a reasoning provider must not be used to infer a replacement merely for convenience (DL-30, DL-93's own text). A Pattern built from a derived attribute must preserve its derivation in its own explanation ("a reasoning provider classified this as jazz," never "genre = jazz" presented as sourced metadata). **12. The Mode/context residual** (refinement 2, above, resolved, not merely narrowed): evidence observed while a household Mode is active remains **eligible**, carrying its Mode context as part of its own ordinary Provenance (already required of every Domain Event); a Pattern, to remain epistemically honest, must be built only from **context-consistent** observations — a Mode-context occurrence and an ordinary-context occurrence are not evidence of the *same* repeated behaviour, so a Pattern spanning both would misrepresent genuine repetition. **No third Continuity scope or new "Mode-scoped learning" tier is created**; this is a direct consequence of the already-required context/provenance fidelity on every Domain Event and the definition of Pattern as repetition of consistent behaviour, not an invented rule. **13. Retention and correction, explicitly deferred, not absorbed**: **OD-26** (#125) owns scope/duration of the resulting evidence/Pattern history, not this decision; a Pattern or Suggestion remains explainable only as long as its cited eligible evidence remains resolvable (**DL-27**/**DL-104**/**DL-111**), reporting **unavailable**, never silently re-rendered, where it has expired; otherwise-expired evidence is never retained merely because a Pattern cites it, absent a separately documented governed gap (DL-42/DL-46 discipline, unchanged). Where attribution is later corrected, the original Domain Event is never rewritten (DL-26/DL-27 immutability; DL-73's "revision is additive"); a corrected observation is a new, additional record; **whether an existing Pattern/Suggestion is recomputed, invalidated, or left standing is OD-28's own lifecycle question, not decided here**. A new eligible observation never silently overwrites an already-accepted preference — it may only form a new Pattern/Suggestion requiring its own fresh acceptance | Foundation, Continuity, Identity, Operational Trust, Concierge | A Learning responsibility of any kind; a second learned-preference store; a new source-attribution taxonomy or confidence vocabulary distinct from DL-73; a Person-plus-Room preference tier; absence of automation evidence treated as manual action; Unknown Person or non-consenting Person activity treated as person-scoped learning evidence; Guest activity converted into resident preference; one-off or accidental activity promoted to Pattern or preference; automation repetition promoted to resident preference; competing residents' evidence averaged, voted, or silently merged into one household preference; DL-100's decorative-presentation-precedence rule applied to operational Room-scoped learning evidence; a fabricated "Room-scoped learned preference" proposal mechanism; a dismissal or silence treated as negative preference evidence or as acceptance; explicit rejection conflated with bare dismissal; repetition promoted to tradition/meaning/significance without the ordinary acceptance step; a reasoning-derived attribute silently promoted to Fact or preference; native Home Assistant history copied merely to preserve learning provenance; a categorical Mode-based exclusion rule, or a new Mode-scoped learning tier; an existing accepted preference silently overwritten by new evidence; OD-26, OD-28, OD-77, or OD-78 decided or absorbed |

This decision governs the inverse: HTBW **publishing** governed capability **into** the platform for a resident's own automations, scripts, blueprints, and dashboards to call — a directionally distinct question, not symmetrical merely because both sides reference Home Assistant, and not resolvable by analogy to the consuming rules alone. **2. General posture, precisely scoped.** A restricted general publishing posture is accepted: a *category* of publishing **may be constitutionally available** under the restrictions below. **This does not mean every eligible-looking value shall be published.** Each child decision retains full responsibility to independently prove semantic fit, surface fit, disclosure safety, retention acceptability, interaction semantics, platform support, and projection lifecycle for its own specific case; this decision supplies only the constitutional boundary those decisions consume. **3. Authority invariant (DL-31 applied, not extended).** For every accepted surface type — service, event, entity, household-object parameter — the determining owning responsibility retains the authoritative value or effect; the published representation is a projection or adapter, never a second authority (restating `stewardship.md`'s already-accepted "An obligation may be projected, but never surrendered" pattern, generalized to every surface type); native Home Assistant state never supersedes HTBW's own constitutional state; a caller cannot acquire authority merely through access to a published service, entity, or event; every system-of-record mutation flows through the owning responsibility's own governed interface, never a bypass. **4. A occurrence is eligible for native publication where it is stable and resident-useful, sourced from an already-governed Domain Event with a declared owner, safely disclosure-gated or non-sensitive by classification, and does not require durable native retention as HTBW's sole record of what happened — HTBW's own Domain Event already carries durable meaning independently under **DL-47**. The resolved target set is never exposed as a durable, raw, authoritative catalog of household structure — this is the only outcome consistent with `contextual-vocabulary.md`'s already-accepted no-write-back rule, not a new invention. Self-consumption — SHOULD converge on a common responsibility-owned governed core; MUST NOT bypass, weaken, or diverge from it (refinement 4, above — two distinct strengths, not one).** Strict identical-transport self-consumption is rejected: it would make Home Assistant's own service registry an undeclared, universal, load-bearing dependency of HTBW's own internal operation, directly contradicting **DL-41**'s own "an undeclared load-bearing dependency is a defect"; it would also degrade caller attribution for purely-internal calls, since **DL-104**'s own independently-verified finding is that automation/script-originated native calls routinely carry `user_id=None` — round-tripping an internal call through that same mechanism worsens attribution HTBW already possesses directly, for no benefit; and it forces inherently private, transactional, multi-step internal operations into an unnatural public contract shape. Minimum conceptual contents, no storage format or tooling selected: stable capability identifier; owning responsibility; purpose in household terms; publication category (service/event/entity/object); contract version; status (active/deprecated/removed); accepted parameters as Declarations/Request-Parameters; result semantics; **DL-76** Action-Risk Class; disclosure class; Decision Trace behavior; availability/degradation; retention consequence; idempotency/retry behavior where applicable; deprecation/migration timeline; and the relationship to any child projection decision. **Catalog coverage for a governed household-object parameter documents, at the owning capability's own entry, that a vocabulary-term parameter type is accepted and how it is conceptually resolved — never a per-term or per-household catalog of actual vocabulary content** (refinement 1, above), which remains prohibited exactly as rule 7 already requires. Public capability contracts create resident/integrator dependencies: additive changes must not break an existing caller; breaking changes require a deprecation notice and migration guidance before removal; **no backward-compatibility promise is made for any legacy service name** (restated, not reopened). Release governance reuses this repository's own existing decision-ledger/formal-acceptance-review discipline and the already-accepted monthly `home-assistant-release-review-standard.md` process; no parallel release process is invented. **10. Automation-first guidance — prospective only, never mandatory migration.** HTBW may recommend that new resident automations prefer governed HTBW capabilities where HTBW owns the relevant semantics (Contextual Vocabulary, Room Context, Continuity, restoration, merged-Room handling, Operational Trust, explainability). **Existing household automations remain valid and are never required to be rewritten, wrapped, or migrated** (**DL-111**/OD-64's existing boundary, restated, not reopened); migration remains optional in every case. **11. Caller attribution must remain truthful.** Native `Context.user_id` retains its native meaning as an authenticated Home Assistant user identifier, independently re-verified terminal across three separate checks (`home-assistant-boundary.md`'s own source-level `Context.__slots__` inspection; **DL-104**'s own independent re-verification against three official external primary sources; the 2026.9 review's own R3 row) — **no native resolved-HTBW-Person field or extension slot exists.** Writing an HTBW-resolved Person into `Context.user_id` is prohibited outright as false attribution, worse than missing attribution; HTBW must not synthesize HA user identity, overwrite `user_id`, map a Person to `user_id` without a separately accepted independent account-linkage decision, or imply native Activity can show the resolved household Person when it structurally cannot — native Activity may truthfully show HTBW as an integration, or another native source classification, never the resolved household Person, unless independently established native authenticated-user evidence genuinely supports it; HTBW's own Decision Trace remains the authoritative place for governed requester/Person attribution. A resident-authored automation calling a published HTBW capability does not, by that fact alone, establish the automation's author as the current requesting Person — no authorship inference is ever made; the Decision Trace records native automation/script origin and any independently-established Person attribution as separate facts, never merged. A caller-supplied Person reference parameter remains a claim, never an Identity Assertion merely because a public contract accepts it (**DL-32**/**DL-38** candidate-exclusion discipline, applied, not reopened); Identity and Operational Trust evaluate it exactly as any other evidence. **12. a **governed external dependency** (configured/authorized/invoked by HA-Prod, whose own compute/storage occurs outside it — "configured by Prod" never means "inside Prod"; OpenAI, Nabu Casa, and any cloud provider are never members regardless of authorization, consent, or encrypted transport, and OD-95 does not own their own consent/enable/disable/replacement lifecycle, which remains each provider class's own governing decision, e.g. **DL-93** for Reasoning); and an **unclassified/unadmitted resource** (reachable, discoverable, even household-owned, but lacking a current admission record — absence of admission, not absence of reachability, controls, so an unknown local server is treated exactly as an external provider for a capability requiring HA-Prod locality). **Connected Storage is not overstated**: Home Assistant's storage-connection abstraction and the declared share/namespace HTBW's own governed namespace lives within are the membership subject; the **backing NAS host is never itself assessed or admitted**, and an unrelated share or service the same physical NAS happens to run is not a member merely by co-location (**DL-42**, **DL-44**, reused, not reopened, corrected from a looser three-way framing to this explicit five-way distinction: host, Home-Assistant storage-connection abstraction, declared share/namespace, the storage subsystem HTBW consumes through, and the consuming HTBW capability). **Granularity is the narrowest unit Home Assistant or HTBW already naturally configures** — never an invented finer atom, never an entire host by default; "Forgotten" is not adopted as a canonical lifecycle state:** as used in the prior issue text it collapsed at least three genuinely distinct governed operations, and is replaced by already-existing vocabulary — **Revocation** (above); **Preference deletion**, a resident-directed removal of the Continuity preference record, governed like any other preference deletion under DL-47's four structural floors and DL-56's "remains effective until explicitly withdrawn, never silently expires" discipline; and **source-evidence expiration**, the underlying Domain Events/Experience History expiring under their own already-governed retention (DL-122, DL-47), entirely independent of whether the preference or permission still exists. Canonical taxonomy, four classes, each with exactly one owner.** **Last Stable Observed Value** — Continuity governs capture eligibility, scope, and explainability over a value Home Assistant itself holds and owns (a Helper or an equivalent native store **#146** later verifies, never copied); captured only where the value has remained unchanged for a household-configured dwell interval **and**, where Person-scoped, DL-73 Known/Probable Source plus Known Person attribution is independently established; Room-scoped capture requires no Person attribution, restating Use Case 1's "none for a room-scoped value"; dwell alone never establishes authorship or preference, restating `behavioral-governance.md`'s resident-versus-automation rule directly. **Configured Default** — a resident-authored declared value, distinct from any observed/remembered value and from a shipped platform default; may exist at Person or Room scope; governed as an ordinary Continuity preference once declared. **Person Preference** and **Room Preference** — the existing, unchanged ordinary Continuity preferences (DL-123's lifecycle where learned; direct household configuration otherwise). **Rejected or collapsed, not separately canonized:** "last observed value" (too noisy; the stability gate is what makes the class governable at all — collapses into Last Stable Observed Value); "last successful value" (ambiguous between an operational memory and an application outcome — collapses into Last Stable Observed Value or the "restored" outcome label, never a source); "Experience preference" (not a third preference tier; a preference about an Experience is filed at whichever of Person/Room scope it actually has — DL-100's two-scope ceiling restated, not reopened); "restored state" (never a source class — an outcome/application-result label only, point 14). **2. HTBW governs only the capture-eligibility rule, the scope, the restoration decision, and the explainability — exactly the governed-meaning residual #146 and DL-46 require, never a second Recorder, never a reconstruction from Recorder/history. Recent native state MAY be consulted at capture time to evaluate dwell-stability — a narrow, bounded lookback distinct from using history as the source of a RESTORED value, which remains prohibited; restated, not reopened. **3. Dwell/stability interval** is a household-configured capture-eligibility parameter; no HTBW-wide default is invented, reusing the now four-times-established "household configures; no invented default" pattern (DL-97, DL-98, DL-107, DL-112). **OD-18/DL-59 (Fact Freshness) is a distinct concern** — current-state validity windows for Truth's own Facts — and does not own this capture-trigger parameter; this decision is its own, narrow owner. Stability alone is never evidence of authorship; DL-73's Source/Person Attribution tiers independently govern who, if anyone, a captured value is attributed to. **4. Device/entity collection within Room scope.** No third scope tier is created. A Room-scoped Last Stable Observed Value MAY be a keyed collection whose members are native target references (for example a Room's remembered lighting collection, keyed by target, each member an independent native Helper/reference) — accepted under this decision as architecture, not merely preserved as rank-4 evidence. The governing scope remains the Room; a keyed member is never a new governance tier. **5. Fan-out restoration** — applying a keyed collection may require one native call per member rather than one call per Room/class; this reuses existing execution/target/partial-application patterns and DL-41's availability model (apply the available subset, name what was withheld), creating no new architectural responsibility. **6. Channel independence** — music volume, duck volume, TTS volume, and the lighting collection (and any other currently canonical Room-scoped channel) remain separately governed and separately captured/restored; none is derived from another without an independently accepted rule; restated, not reopened. **7. Room temperature** is explicitly **in scope** as a Room-scoped Last Stable Observed Value, governed identically to every other channel: captured via the same dwell/attribution rule, restored subject to the same precondition set (point 9), and never permitted to override a live safety/HVAC/Operational-Trust constraint — a remembered temperature is a candidate value, never an instruction that bypasses present authority. **8. Restoration semantics.** **Reproduction is the default and only mode this decision authorizes:** the Home attempts to apply the governed remembered value unchanged, subject to the precondition set. **Derivation is not authorized by this decision for any value class** — no capability is named as an authorized deriver; where a future capability is separately accepted to derive a value, it must be recorded, explained, and Decision-Trace-labelled as a derivation, never narrated as the remembered value, and must never silently substitute for a failed reproduction. **9. Precondition set**, applied before reproduction, each an already-accepted mechanism and no new category: current Truth (including environmental-constraint Facts), Room mode, Identity Band where Person-scoped, Operational Trust's authorization outcome, audience composition, safety, and target/capability availability (DL-41). Where any precondition fails, the Home does not apply the remembered value and does not silently substitute a computed or platform value; it states why, naming the specific precondition. **10. Three distinct absent/invalid states, never collapsed:** (a) no remembered value has ever been captured; (b) a remembered value exists but its native source is currently unreadable/unavailable (DL-41's unavailable-dependency outcome, never silently defaulted); (c) a remembered value exists, is readable, and is valid, but a precondition currently makes restoration inappropriate (point 9). **11. Platform/shipped defaults are never memory** — never represented as remembered, preferred, selected, or accepted; a legitimately used non-memory fallback is explained as exactly that, never as restoration. **12. Accepted Adaptive Policy output is not "last person-selected"** — restates DL-123 directly: a value the Home applied autonomously under an accepted Adaptive Policy is attributed as an HTBW learned/adaptive-policy Decision Authority (DL-73), never narrated as a direct Person selection merely because the Person originally accepted the policy; where that applied value later becomes capture-eligible, ordinary DL-73/DL-112 attribution rules apply exactly as to any other observation, producing the Adaptive Policy's own Decision Authority as the evidence basis, never a fabricated direct-selection record. **13. Merged Room** reuses, rather than reinvents, the already-accepted DL-13/DL-62 Primary-Authority-selection discipline Room Configuration already applies to Environmental Purpose: for each remembered-value channel, exactly one constituent Room is the Merged Room's selected source; a restoration addressed to the Merged Room reads/writes through to that one selected constituent Room's own record; a direct action addressed to a specific constituent Room continues to use that Room's own record, entirely unaffected. No separate "Merged Room memory" object is created and no new deterministic-priority algorithm is invented: because a non-selected constituent Room's own record is never touched by a Merged-Room interaction, exiting the merged context cannot destroy it — the invariant is structural. **14. Restored output must not self-reinforce** — applying a reproduced remembered value and observing the resulting state remain stable for the dwell interval does not by itself regenerate capture evidence; DL-112's existing evidence-eligibility rules (automation-generated/system-applied values are operational evidence only, never preference evidence merely because they were tolerated or remained stable) already structurally prevent this. A subsequent, genuinely eligible resident correction remains ordinary DL-112 evidence, unchanged. **15. Retention under DL-47** — the native Helper/entity value is Home Assistant's own object, outside DL-47's HTBW-governed-record taxonomy (DL-46); HTBW declares no retention for it because HTBW does not hold it. Any HTBW-governed reference or scope assignment is a Current Projection (replaced, never retained) with history expressed as ordinary Change Records exactly as any other Continuity preference; a Decision Trace follows DL-47's existing rule unchanged. No new retained-value history, second store, or history owner is created. **16. Read. May seed a term" rule, unchanged) and passes the resolved native Floor identifier straight through as a native target — **execution fan-out is the platform's own documented behaviour, never an HTBW-authored enumeration of constituent Areas**. OD-04's remaining questions (same-scope conflict resolution, competing-Communication ordering, safety-category placement, the `undecidable` outcome) are untouched and remain entirely OD-04's own. **6. Floor is not a first-class Truth subject; no Floor Fact and no "Floor health" is created.** Foundation's own accepted object-type enumeration (`foundation-contract.md`) does not include Floor, and this decision does not add it. A query such as *"What's the temperature upstairs"* or *"Are any windows upstairs open"* is answered as a **Concierge-assembled projection over each constituent Room's own already-existing Primary-Authority Fact (DL-62)** — reusing the identical "Concierge-assembled projection, not a decision HTBW made" discipline DL-74 already established for Historical Reconstruction — presented per constituent Room, never silently blended into one synthetic Floor-level value; DL-60/DL-62's existing rejection of same-purpose Composite-Contributor aggregation at Room scope extends identically to Floor, for the identical reason. **7. Floor and Merged Room are semantically distinct, not newly decided but now made explicit as OD-10's own finding**: Merged Room is an HTBW-owned, curated interaction and vocabulary context (persona, participation, exclusions, DL-67); Floor is Home Assistant's own native physical hierarchy serving broader native targeting. | **DL-126** | **Accepted 2026-11-03 (Issue #97, formal acceptance review PASS; no further remediation required).** **Policy Precedence Order, Most-Restrictive Combination, and Competing-Communication Ordering.** Resolves **OD-04** in full, consuming **DL-125** (Floor), **DL-76** (Action-Risk Class), **DL-77** (Urgency), **DL-78** (Category), **DL-75** (Significance), **DL-97** (escalation, OD-22), **DL-13** (Room/Merged Room equivalence), **DL-74/DL-60/DL-62** (projection/Primary-Authority discipline), and **DL-112** (no averaging/merging) unchanged — none is reopened. **1. Four-operation decomposition adopted as a restatement of existing responsibility boundaries, inventing no new mechanism:** (A) Candidate Value/Preference Resolution — Continuity, consuming DL-123/DL-124's value-class model unchanged; (B) Authority/Policy Ceiling Evaluation — Operational Trust, the ceiling rule and the five-outcome authority model; (C) Current Explicit Request — an input to (A), never itself a scope or a ceiling bypass; (D) Competing-Communication Ordering — Concierge, applying only to Communications whose authority outcome already cleared (B). **2. The scope-and-precedence list is reaffirmed, not reinvented:** `operational-trust.md`'s existing table — Home, Room (including Merged Room, behaving identically, DL-13 — no Room-vs-Merged-Room precedence tier is created), Person, Asset, Relationship, Experience class, Action-Risk Class, External Decision Authority — is unchanged and sufficient; Floor remains excluded (DL-125). **3. Mode is not a first-class scope.** Mode is a governed Room- or Home-scoped Truth fact (`nighttime-suppression.md` Scenario 1) that selects which Room/Home policy applies; it is an applicability/condition dimension, never an independent ownership scope; "Mode-owned policy" is rejected. **4. Capability and operation are not scopes; both are applicability/condition dimensions.** A capability declares the Action-Risk Class that governs it (DL-76's Capability Default tier); Operation Type (Read/Write/Delete/Govern, DL-36/DL-76) is the independent axis selecting which threshold within a Risk Class applies; neither is added to the scope list. **5. Person is dual in kind, never dual in precedence.** A Person-scoped statement is either a Policy (ceiling-relevant — child safety, guest limitation — authored under Operational Trust) or a Preference (candidate-value-relevant only — genre, artist — authored under Continuity), per `behavioral-governance.md`'s existing ownership rules; **a Person preference never becomes a ceiling and never becomes permission** (DL-36, restated). **6. Home is the already-existing Operational Trust household-wide scope** (quiet hours, away mode, global autonomy ceiling) plus Continuity's household-level default preference; no second "global" concept is created. **7. Most-restrictive combination is precise, not rhetorical.** Across every applicable scope, each yields one of the five accepted outcomes (`permitted`, `prohibited`, `permitted_with_confirmation`, `permitted_with_escalation`, `undecidable`): (i) any applicable `prohibited` makes the final outcome `prohibited`; (ii) absent (i), any applicable `undecidable` makes the final outcome `undecidable` — never rendered as `permitted`; (iii) absent (i) and (ii), every applicable `permitted_with_confirmation` and `permitted_with_escalation` requirement combines cumulatively — each is independently discharged, and satisfying one never substitutes for another (restates DL-36 directly); (iv) only if every applicable scope yields `permitted` does the final outcome become `permitted`, at the most restrictive applicable autonomy level. A narrower scope's `permitted` never cancels a broader or otherwise-applicable scope's more restrictive outcome. **8. Same-scope conflict resolution:** two versions of the same governed policy are temporal/current-projection semantics, never a precedence contest (DL-27/P29/P30 unchanged; Decision Trace cites the exact version in force); two independent applicable policies at the same scope combine under clause 7 exactly as across scopes, never by arbitrary arrival order; two candidate preferences at the same scope (Operation A) resolve by specificity/current-intent, never by granting either permission; two simultaneously eligible Communications resolve under clause 14, never the policy-scope ladder. **9. Explicit current request (Operation C).** A current explicit request outranks a stored preference as evidence of present intent within Operation A; it never outranks an applicable ceiling, confirmation, escalation, or safety/privacy restriction evaluated in Operation B. **10. Safety creates no new responsibility or tier.** Safety is expressed entirely through the Safety Action-Risk Class (DL-76), the Safety Communication Category (DL-78, content-domain only, never a severity rank), Experience-class-scoped suppression exceptions (`nighttime-suppression.md` Scenario 4 — "Suppression policy is scoped by experience class. Media may be suppressed while care escalations are not"), and clause 7's ceiling combination; HTBW asserts no life-safety capability it does not have (DL-79 restated). **11. `undecidable` is never a weaker policy.** Restates `operational-trust-contract.md`'s enum unchanged: `undecidable` is never rendered `permitted`; it is reported naming the specific unresolved scope or input, never silently dropped in favour of another applicable scope's `permitted`. **12. Safe default versus deterministic refusal.** This decision introduces no platform-wide safe-default outcome; where clause 7 yields only `prohibited`/`undecidable`, the result is an explicitly labelled refusal or `undecidable` — never attributed to a Person, Room, or household preference. **13. Bounded wait/re-evaluate is a Concierge execution strategy**, applied to an `undecidable` (Abstain) outcome under an Action-Risk Class permitting re-evaluation — never a new scope, outcome, or Communication-ordering tier; it reuses DL-77 Section 11's reevaluation discipline by direct analogy, and the bound and its re-evaluation are recorded in Decision Trace. **14. Competing-Communication ordering is a separate, deterministic algorithm, never the policy-scope ladder:** (i) eligibility gate — only Communications whose authority outcome is not `prohibited`/`undecidable`, and whose DL-77 Urgency currently permits the interruption, compete; (ii) Urgency (DL-77's fixed ladder) is the primary discriminator; (iii) where Urgency ties, Significance (the Communication's existing Significance reference to Stewardship's Base Significance, DL-75: Routine < Important < Significant < Critical) is the secondary discriminator, reused unmodified; (iv) where both tie, this is the already-recognised "Equal-priority policies" conflict class (`behavioral-governance.md`'s own Conflict-resolution table): the household configures the deterministic tie-break; **no HTBW-wide default order is invented**, and completing that configuration surface is a distinct follow-on question, not an Owner Policy Question, tracked under **OD-47**; (v) Category (DL-78) plays no role in ordering; (vi) Defer and Redirect remain Concierge's expression of Operational Trust's underlying constraint (`operational-trust.md`'s six-outcome table, unchanged) — ordering never upgrades a Deferred/Redirected Communication into presented, and Defer/Redirect are never relocated into Operational Trust; (vii) where required ordering context cannot be resolved, `undecidable` withholds the Communication rather than defaulting it into presentation or an arbitrary position. **15. Scenario reproducibility confirmed, none altered:** `nighttime-suppression.md` Scenarios 1-6 and `multi-person-conflict.md` Scenarios 1, 2, 5, and 6 reproduce their documented outcomes exactly under clauses 7-14. **16. | **DL-127** | **Accepted 2026-11-03 (Issue #123, formal acceptance review PASS; no further remediation required).** **Session Contention Outcomes — No Merge Construct, Intent-Anchoring Transitions, and Multi-Room Target Expansion.** Resolves **OD-24** in full, consuming **DL-102** (OD-27) and **DL-126** (OD-04) unchanged — neither is reopened. **1. No Session Merge construct exists (Option B).** HTBW does not combine two Sessions into one synthetic merged Session, ever. Every historical "merge" scenario is already covered by distinct, already-named mechanisms: participant join (an explicit Operational-Trust-evaluated act, DL-102), displacement (Operational Trust's own authority, `multi-person-conflict.md` Rule 3), transfer suppression (the existing Transfer lifecycle's "suppressed transfer" outcome, DL-102), grouped playback within one Merged Room (DL-13/DL-102, one Session, one Current Room), and multi-Room target expansion (clause 6, below). "Merge" is retired as an architectural noun for Session concurrency; competing intent is resolved by one of these named outcomes, never invented merge mechanics. **2. What "merge" historically meant, now fully discharged.** The open question Episode 7/#151 and DL-102's own export left to OD-24 — what happens when a Transfer or fresh request's owner/participant resolution contends with an incumbent Session — is answered entirely by clause 1 plus DL-102's existing outcomes (suppressed transfer; conflict-reported-not-started) plus Operational Trust's displacement authority. No further mechanics are required. **3. Person-following versus Room-anchored intent uses the existing Transfer-intent field, never a new Session subtype.** `experience-and-session.md` already carries Transfer intent (Follow-Me, ask-before-transfer, never-transfer) as an ordinary Session element. "Leave it here" is a Change Record mutating the active Session's own Transfer intent to never-transfer (Follow-Me eligibility ends for this Session going forward); "take it with me" is a Change Record mutating Transfer intent to Follow-Me, requiring no known destination at the moment of the request. Both reuse the general governed-record Current-Projection-plus-Change-Record pattern already used for every other Session-state transition (Starting-to-Active-to-...-to-Ended, and Ended-back-to-Active via Resume): **the Session's own Record Identity never changes, no successor Session is created, and no historical meaning is rewritten.** This uses current authority's own established mutation pattern in preference to ending-and-recreating a Session, because the existing Change Record history already supplies equivalent explainability. **4. An explicit Room-targeted command is Room-anchored by default.** "Play music in my Office" establishes an ordinary Session with Transfer intent never-transfer, because Follow-Me was never invoked; the Person subsequently leaving the Room is never, by itself, reason to transfer, follow, or end that Session — occupancy is not a universal termination mechanism, and intent provenance (clause 3), not mere observed presence, governs Session lifecycle. **5. Playback left behind pending an ineligible Follow-Me transfer reuses the existing Session lifecycle and Resume-eligibility-window field unchanged; the governing duration is OD-25's own** (Resume Eligibility Window Defaults, #124, still open), not invented here. Identity supplies presence/location evidence; Continuity consumes it and never recomputes or manufactures it. **6. Multi-Room target expansion creates no Floor/House/"everywhere"-owned Session tier.** "Throughout the house," "upstairs," and similar phrases are Concierge/vocabulary target resolution (contextual-vocabulary.md's Home-scoped term resolution and/or native Home Assistant multi-Area/Floor targeting) producing N independently targeted Rooms — directly reusing **DL-125**'s own "Floor-targeted fan-out, each entity's own scope evaluated independently" precedent by direct analogy. Each resulting Room receives its own ordinary per-Room Session, independently governed; a later Room-specific command (for example, "turn the music down in the Den") affects only that Room's own Session, never reaching into the other Rooms the earlier broad command also targeted. The earlier broad command remains Decision Trace provenance for why each Room's Session began; it does not bind the resulting per-Room Sessions into one Session. **7. Target resolution and value resolution are separate operations, consuming DL-124 and DL-126 unchanged.** Once a target expression resolves to Rooms (clause 6), each Room resolves its own applicable value (for example, volume) under existing Continuity/DL-124 rules unless the current explicit request itself supplies an explicit value, which is DL-126's own Candidate Resolution/Current Explicit Request operation, applied per targeted Room. **8. Remembered-value observation is a structurally independent governed activity, restating DL-124, not reopened.** A command causing a Room's observable state to change is one governed activity; an independent remembered-value observer separately, later, evaluates whether the new state qualifies as stable under DL-124's own dwell/attribution gating and records it if so. Causation never merges the two activities into one Session, and the causing Session/command is never recorded as the owner of the resulting remembered-value record. **9. Participant join remains distinct, restating DL-102 unchanged.** Co-presence is never itself a participant fact; an explicit Operational-Trust-evaluated join is required; Session count remains one. **10. Grouped/synchronized provider-level playback spanning separate, non-merged Rooms remains DL-102's own narrow, explicitly deferred residual** — not decided here, and not to be confused with multi-Room target expansion (clause 6), which produces independent per-Room Sessions rather than one synchronized cross-Room session. **11. Duplicate playback restates DL-102's existing semantic-only guarantee unchanged.** Intentional multi-Room playback (clause 6) and intentional Merged-Room/grouped playback (DL-13/DL-102) are each legitimate, already-distinguished patterns and must never be misclassified as accidental duplication; no blanket "never play in two Rooms" rule is created. **12. Merged Room remains entirely unaffected.** Movement within a Merged Room remains neither Transfer nor Resume (DL-13, restated, not reopened); nothing above alters that. **13. Scope boundary — validated, not absorbed.** The automation-versus-explicit-intent courtesy scenario (for example, Den shades) is already fully resolved by **DL-126**'s own "current explicit intent may supersede stored/default outcome within Candidate Resolution, but never bypasses an applicable ceiling" plus the existing Ask-versus-Assume rule — confirmed by validation, requiring no new Session-specific mechanism. **The timeout-never-creates-authority principle is a direct corollary of DL-126's existing undecidable/ceiling semantics applied to the temporal dimension, not a new mechanism.** **A Room-scoped temporary manual-override grace period (what remains in effect after a Room becomes unoccupied, and for how long) has no existing canonical representation anywhere in the repository searched** (`room-configuration.md`, `continuity.md`, `operational-trust.md`); this is a genuine gap, **not decided, invented, or defaulted under OD-24** — it does not concern Session merge or concurrency, and is routed to Epic #147 as a candidate new issue, consistent with this decision's own scope-control requirement. **14. Decision Trace requires no new field.** `experience-and-session.md`'s existing session-state-transition discipline already requires every transition to carry its Decision Trace reference; this decision names participant join, displacement refusal, transfer suppression, Transfer-intent mutation, and multi-Room target-expansion provenance as transition kinds already covered, inventing no new mechanism | A synthetic merged Session construct; two Sessions combined into one record; a Session's own Record Identity changed or a successor Session created for an ordinary Transfer-intent mutation; occupancy alone ending a Room-anchored (never-transfer) Session; a Person-continuity or manual-override-grace numeric default invented here; a Floor/House/"everywhere"-owned Session-ownership tier; multi-Room target expansion treated as one synchronized cross-Room session; legitimate multi-Room or Merged-Room playback misclassified as accidental duplication; remembered-value observation coupled to or attributed to the causing Session; provider-level session-handoff mechanics invented; a Room post-occupancy manual-override grace period invented, defaulted, or decided under OD-24; the shade/automation courtesy-ask scenario redecided here instead of citing DL-126 | [../models/experience-and-session.md](../models/experience-and-session.md), [../models/continuity.md](../models/continuity.md), [../contracts/continuity-contract.md](../contracts/continuity-contract.md), [../scenarios/multi-person-conflict.md](../scenarios/multi-person-conflict.md), [../scenarios/continuity-use-cases.md](../scenarios/continuity-use-cases.md), [../scenarios/follow-me-media.md](../scenarios/follow-me-media.md) |
| **DL-128** | **Accepted 2026-11-03 (Issue #124, formal acceptance review PASS; no further remediation required).** **Follow-Me as Explicit Current Intent — Superseding Time-Based Resume Eligibility Windows.** Resolves **OD-25** in full (SUPERSEDE/REFRAME, Option B), consuming **DL-122** (OD-26), **DL-126** (OD-04), and **DL-127** (OD-24) unchanged — none is reopened. **1. The original premise is superseded.** "Resume Eligibility Window Defaults" — a time-based, per-experience-class default duration governing when HTBW may proactively offer a historical resume — is retired. The window existed to gate a proactive suggestion behaviour the Owner has now rejected outright (no unsolicited "you left X, continue here?"); absent that behaviour, there is nothing left for a time window to gate. No per-class durations are defined, and none are needed. **2. Two previously conflated lifecycle dimensions are separated.** (a) A **pending Follow-Me intent** for a currently **active** experience; (b) **resuming an ended Session** by a fresh explicit request. Each has its own already-sufficient governance, below. **3. Pending Follow-Me intent is lifecycle-bound, never time-bound.** CURRENT (an active, eligible experience exists) → PENDING (an explicit Follow-Me request established intent) → **SETTLED** (successfully continued somewhere) | **CANCELLED** (explicitly withdrawn) | **SUPERSEDED** (a newer Follow-Me request for a different active experience replaced it) | **BLOCKED** (a governed condition currently prevents settlement, attribution preserved, remains pending). Simple elapsed time is never, by itself, a reason to drop a pending intent — there is no "expired" state for Follow-Me. **4. One pending Follow-Me intent per Person, by direct analogy to DL-102's one-owner-per-Session discipline.** A new Follow-Me request for a different active experience supersedes any still-pending prior intent for that Person, reusing the existing Governed-Reference Supersedes/Superseded-by pattern (already used for Communications) rather than inventing a new one; the superseded intent is retained only as ordinary history — never queued, never re-offered, never surfaced as a backlog. **5. Resuming an ended Session by explicit request needs no new duration.** Its availability is already fully governed by **DL-122**'s Experience History retention (Room Setup/Person Setup configured floor/ceiling; DL-122 explicitly retains "session ownership, participants, transfer, and resume outcomes") plus **DL-46**'s provider-owned content/position availability. No additional, HTBW-side, per-experience-class resume duration is created; where DL-122's retention has made the record unavailable, the explicit request is answered as unavailable, exactly as DL-122 already requires. **6. Disambiguation of an unqualified "follow me."** Exactly one current, active, eligible experience → Concierge may resolve it without asking. More than one → Concierge asks, never guesses, restating the existing Ask-versus-Assume/ambiguity-is-first-class-output discipline by direct analogy to experience selection. None → Follow-Me establishes nothing; HTBW never searches Experience History or provider history to manufacture a candidate. **7. Destination may be unresolved or explicitly supplied at initiation, using one representation.** "Follow me with the music" leaves the destination to resolve later (via Identity evidence or an explicit "resume here," DL-127 unchanged); "follow me with the music to the Den" supplies the destination immediately as current-intent/target-context evidence, resolved through the already-canonical Room Context mechanism — never requiring a later "resume here" merely to (re)identify the destination it already named. **An explicit destination is evidence of where the Person wants the experience to continue, never evidence of where the Person currently is** — it is never treated as an Identity-derived presence assertion, and it never bypasses Operational Trust, capability, availability, provider, or privacy governance. **8. No new governed-record class or Session field is created.** The pending Follow-Me intent is represented entirely by the Session's own existing fields: Transfer intent (Follow-Me, DL-127, unchanged), Resume eligibility (its semantics now carry the lifecycle state of clause 3 rather than a time-window value), and Blocking state (existing, DL-102/DL-127). **9. Two stale worked examples are corrected, not reopened as architecture.** `continuity.md`'s "Worked examples" and `continuity.md`/`continuity-contract.md`'s "Three modes" table each depicted an unprompted historical resume offer ("You left a documentary in the Primary Bedroom. Move it here?") as a canonical Assisted-mode illustration. Neither was its own Decision Ledger entry; both are corrected to depict Assisted mode confirming an **already-pending explicit Follow-Me intent**, never fabricating one from mere historical activity. **10. No unfinished-content catalog, Journey, checkpoint, or progress-marker object exists**, restating `continuity-contract.md`'s and `continuity-use-cases.md` Use Case 4's own existing prohibition unchanged, now extended: the time-window concept that previously sat beside that prohibition is itself retired by clause 1. **11. Provider-position boundary is unchanged (DL-46, P21).** The provider remains authoritative for playback position and content availability; a disagreeing remembered Governed Reference never overrides it, restating Use Case 4 Scenario 4.3 unchanged. **12. The #148/OD-77 dependency is narrowed, not resolved.** This decision's core lifecycle never requires Person-to-provider-account association: Session ownership is already Identity/Operational-Trust-governed (DL-102, DL-127) independent of which provider account backs the content, so the pending-Follow-Me-intent model closes without it. The narrower, still-open question — whose progress is whose when a household shares one provider account — is untouched and remains entirely **OD-77**'s own; verified **#148/OD-77 remains OPEN** and is not decided here *(Update, 2026-11-05, not a reopening: OD-77 has since closed as **DL-139**, resolving this narrower question — see DL-139's own §12)*. **13. Follow-Me eligibility per Experience class is not decided here.** `experience-and-session.md`'s Experience-class table (Media, Informational, Environmental, Routine, Conversational, Care) carries no Follow-Me-eligibility flag today; whether Briefing/Routine/Care classes are Follow-Me-eligible at all is a genuine, separate classification gap, not invented under OD-25 — it belongs, if ever decided, alongside Room Configuration's existing per-Experience capability declaration, and is routed to Epic #147. **14. Original OD-25 acceptance criteria, fully reconciled:** default windows per class — **superseded**; time- vs. event-bounded expiry — **superseded** (lifecycle events of clause 3 replace elapsed time); Person- vs. Room-scoped differences — **transformed** (pending Follow-Me intent is inherently Person-scoped, one per Person; Room-scoped "last state" continuity remains DL-124's own, untouched); expired-candidate handling — **superseded** for Follow-Me (no "expired" state; clause 3's four terminal states govern), **still applicable** for Experience History under DL-122 unchanged; household configurability — **superseded** as a duration surface (nothing to configure), **still applicable** as Explicit/Assisted/Autonomous mode configuration (Operational Trust's, unchanged); blocked/expired/absent distinguishability — **transformed** into Blocked/Cancelled/Superseded/Settled/Absent, each independently explainable; native media position not duplicated — **still applicable**, restated unchanged (clause 11). **15. Decision Trace requires no new field.** The existing fields (1-2 request/requester, 5 Room Context, 10-11 preferences/continuity intent) already distinguish explicit-destination provenance from Identity-derived-location provenance, and already carry pending/settled/cancelled/superseded/blocked attribution exactly as every other Session-state transition already requires (DL-127, unchanged) | A per-experience-class time-based resume-eligibility default invented or numbered; an unsolicited historical resume offer, or any proactive suggestion mined from provider/Experience history; a resume-candidate backlog, queue, or catalog of unfinished content; a Journey, checkpoint, or progress-marker object; more than one simultaneously pending Follow-Me intent per Person; an "expired" state applied to a pending Follow-Me intent; a destination requirement at Follow-Me initiation; an explicit destination treated as Identity-derived physical presence, or as bypassing Operational Trust/capability/availability/provider/privacy governance; a new Session field or governed-record class for Follow-Me state; the stale unprompted-offer worked examples left standing as current authority; a duplicated provider playback position; #148/OD-77 decided, narrowed beyond clause 12, or assumed resolved; a universal Follow-Me-eligibility rule applied to every Experience class without authority | [../models/continuity.md](../models/continuity.md), [../contracts/continuity-contract.md](../contracts/continuity-contract.md), [../models/experience-and-session.md](../models/experience-and-session.md), [../scenarios/continuity-use-cases.md](../scenarios/continuity-use-cases.md), [../scenarios/follow-me-media.md](../scenarios/follow-me-media.md) |
| **DL-129** | **Accepted 2026-11-04 (Issue #79, formal acceptance review PASS; no further remediation required).** **Decision Trace Persistence — Write-Time Assembly, Connected Storage Authority, Room Normalization, and Storage-Outage Independence.** Resolves **OD-29** in full, consuming **DL-92** (OD-01), **DL-104** (OD-38), and **DL-122** (OD-26) unchanged — none is reopened; preserves **DL-15**, **DL-27**, **DL-31**, **DL-41**, **DL-44**, **DL-46**, **DL-47** unchanged. **1. Authoritative location: Connected Storage, reusing DL-92's persistence mechanism, never a competing one.** The Decision Trace is persisted durably in Connected Storage (one governed JSON-backed record class per DL-92's already-accepted Storage-helper-based mechanism, deployed as the already-accepted External History Retention extension, DL-42, because Decision Trace needs longer-than-native-practical retention, no per-record purge exemption natively, and a structured record native Activity cannot represent — exactly the gap connected-storage.md already lists). Native Home Assistant Activity/Logbook is never the authoritative Decision Trace; no second Explainability model, no second Recorder, no HTBW Activity responsibility or store is created. **2. Durable Decision Trace capture is therefore a Connected-Storage capability dependency (DL-41), and this governs only itself.** Where Connected Storage is absent or unconfigured, durable Decision Trace persistence is `unavailable` as an ordinary dependency outcome — reported, never rendered as a trust, identity, or permission failure. **CRITICAL: this never stops the underlying governed action, non-action, suppression, or refusal from proceeding according to its own governance.** Explainability capture and the Home's governed operation are separate; a storage-dependent capability that itself requires storage (for example, saving an Asset document) still depends on storage per DL-41 unchanged — only durable trace *persistence* degrades, never the decision the trace would have explained. **3. Purge exemption and retention.** Native Recorder offers no per-record purge exemption (reaffirmed, not reopened — #146). A Connected-Storage-held Decision Trace follows its own Explainability retention (values remain OD-05's own, not decided here) plus DL-47's four existing structural floors (Tombstones, consent-lifecycle records, Preservation Hold, governed versions required to keep a held trace explainable) — no competing mechanism invented. Preservation Hold's own authority/duration/review/release remains entirely OD-39's own. **4. Explainability is assembled at write time, consuming DL-27/DL-46 exactly as already accepted — not reinterpreted.** A Decision Trace is composed by Concierge *when the governed evaluation occurs*, consuming each contributing responsibility's own already-accepted record (a Truth Fact's Subject/Statement/confidence/Provenance/Freshness at that moment, an Identity Assertion, a policy version) via DL-104's Governed Reference, exact-version-pinned. Later retrieval of "why did that happen" normally retrieves this already-assembled trace; it does not normally rediscover Room architecture, rerun historical policy, or reconstruct the decision from whatever native evidence survives. **5. DL-27's "references, not copies" is reconciled precisely, restating DL-46 unchanged, never silently redefined.** Prohibited: duplicating the raw native history stream (a lux sensor's full reading series, a Recorder row, a sensor payload) as a parallel HTBW-held copy. Permitted, and already-accepted: the Decision Trace states the material *evaluated* Fact values/thresholds a governed evaluation actually used (such as "735 lux, threshold 800") as constituent content of the trace itself, because that value is the content of Truth's own already-governed, already-versioned Fact — referenced via Governed Reference, never a Recorder-row copy. A retained trace therefore remains explainable after native Recorder/Activity expiry without requiring that ephemeral native evidence still exist. **6. Unresolvable-reference behaviour restates decision-trace.md's existing Failure behavior table unchanged, inventing no new taxonomy:** a dangling reference is reported unavailable with its reason where known; a purged or redacted referenced record resolves to "no longer retained" or "redacted," never "never existed"; a held trace's required references being removed is reported as a preservation failure. A referenced governed artifact is never silently substituted with a current version when a different version governed the historical decision. **7. Evaluation-triggered capture, restating DL-15 precisely.** A Decision Trace is created when HTBW *participates in a governed evaluation* — never merely because a raw entity or sensor state changed. A repeated sensor fluctuation causing no governed evaluation creates no trace (Home Assistant's own history is sufficient). A governed evaluation that results in no action still creates a trace (the non-action is the explainable event). A governed evaluation resulting in suppression, refusal, or intentional silence each creates a trace distinguishing that outcome from the others, reusing the existing **Intentional Non-Action** first-class outcome (glossary) plus its own stated reason — no new outcome-taxonomy names (such as non-canonical legacy EXECUTE_SUCCESS/SILENCE_SUCCESS vocabulary, rank-four evidence, held non-canonical) are adopted; the existing vocabulary, applied consistently with a populated reason field, already prevents calm operation from becoming indistinguishable from suppression or failure. **8. Action issued is not outcome observed — remediates the Episode 9 documentation defect, not a new Owner decision.** `decision-trace.md`'s Required Structure gains a distinct **observed outcome** element after *Action taken*, with `unknown` as a first-class value; a command successfully issued is never treated as proof its physical effect occurred, and is never rendered as failure unless the platform itself reported one. `failure-and-degradation.md` gains the corresponding row: a command issued with no corresponding confirmed state change records the outcome as `unknown`. This directly extends, not duplicates, the existing Communication-specific rule ("never infer Presented from Delivered"). **9. Activity projection is conditional, never manufactured.** Where a governed evaluation results in an action with a corresponding native state change, native Activity's own already-improved execution-causality presentation (2026.9, see clause 16) may be referenced as supporting evidence, consumed by Governed Reference where retrievable and retained (#146 item 6). Where a trace is non-action, suppression, refusal, or evaluation-only with no native state change, no Activity entry is manufactured merely to represent that the trace exists — Home Assistant owns Activity; HTBW owns Decision Trace. **10. Diagnostic fallback is explicitly distinguished from a retained trace, never masquerading as one.** Where no retained Decision Trace exists (never configured, expired under its own retention, lost to an outage, or the event was never an HTBW-governed evaluation), HTBW may assemble a diagnostic explanation at query time from currently available Home Assistant evidence — inspecting applicable current automations/scripts, available current or retained evidence, and stating unavailable evidence honestly. **This diagnostic result is never represented as the missing contemporaneous trace.** Where durable storage is available at query time, the diagnostic interaction itself may be persisted as an ordinary new governed record of a *current* diagnostic activity — recording the question, the time of explanation, systems inspected, evidence available/unavailable, the diagnostic result, and that it was reconstructed at query time rather than contemporaneously captured — never backdated or relabeled as the original trace. **11. External-storage outage produces an honest coverage-gap record on recovery, never fabricated traces.** When Connected Storage returns after an outage, Explainability creates a durable recovery/gap record identifying the affected interval with only the temporal precision the evidence actually supports (a known last-successful write, or a Truth-held storage-unavailable Fact, where either exists) — it never invents an exact boundary it does not have evidence for, and it never retroactively fabricates traces for the gap. A later question about an event inside that interval is answered honestly: durable Explainability coverage was unavailable for that interval, and HTBW may attempt the clause-10 diagnostic fallback from surviving evidence, never presented as the missing historical trace. **12. External-storage availability is one shared capability-dependency condition, restating DL-41 exactly, not reimplemented per responsibility.** No new storage-health mechanism, NAS-health protocol, or per-responsibility availability concept is created. Truth may hold a Fact about Connected-Storage dependency health and Repairs may surface the defect, exactly as DL-41 already allows, without either becoming the owner of the capability or its dependency declaration — restated, not reopened. Because Explainability writes on every governed evaluation, it may often be the first responsibility to detect an outage through ordinary use; detection-through-use never makes Explainability the architectural owner of storage health, and every other storage-dependent responsibility (Asset documents, voiceprints) consumes the same shared availability condition rather than independently rediscovering the same outage. **13. A storage-outage household alert is root-cause-first, reusing existing Communication/Concierge architecture unchanged.** "External storage is unavailable" is the lead fact; the currently *configured and affected* storage-dependent capabilities are named from current configuration, never a hard-coded list; delivery reuses the existing Category/Urgency/Significance/competing-Communication-ordering architecture (**DL-76**, **DL-77**, **DL-78**, **DL-126**) unchanged — no new communication priority system is created, and the household receives one coherent notification rather than separate uncoordinated alerts per affected capability. **14. Explainability retention is independent of Home Assistant Recorder retention, and is configured at two scopes only — no numeric defaults decided here.** Integration Setup carries an Explainability Retention default; Room Setup may override it per Room, reusing DL-122's already-accepted "hybrid of enumerated presets plus a custom numeric override, configured in Room Setup/Person Setup, never globally" pattern by direct analogy; the exact preset labels/values remain OD-05's own. Explainability retention and Recorder retention may differ arbitrarily and are never coupled. **15. Multi-Room commands produce Room-normalized traces, never a Floor/House-owned trace, by direct analogy to DL-125/DL-127.** "Turn off all downstairs lights" produces one Decision Trace per participating Room, each scoped to that Room's own targets, evaluation, and outcome, each governed by that Room's own configured Explainability retention — never a single macro-command record and never a Floor- or House-owned Explainability scope. **16. Cross-Room correlation is retrieval over already-persisted authoritative records, consuming DL-104 unchanged, never diagnostic reconstruction.** Every Room-normalized trace from one originating command carries the same correlation/causation identifier (DL-104); "what was everything impacted by my command last night" is an aggregation query across the authoritative Room traces that still exist. Where Rooms carry different configured retention, some correlated Room traces may have already expired while others remain: the query returns only the available authoritative records, never fabricates a missing Room's outcome, and states that correlated coverage is incomplete wherever that can be established from existing evidence — informing, not deciding, OD-35's own historical-retrieval-surface design. **17. Home Assistant Activity's 2026.9 execution-causality improvement is accurately reconciled, correcting three stale statements, not preserved as obsolete.** Activity now presents what triggered a change, the automations/scripts passed through, and the entity's own change, each step navigable (2026.9, already recorded as finding R1 in `home-assistant-boundary.md`). "Activity records what changed and never why" is narrowed, not retracted: Activity now satisfies **execution causality**; it still carries no identity assertion or confidence, no evidence or provenance, no household governance context, no Operational Trust evaluation, no alternatives considered, and no policy version applied — the Decision Trace's own justification narrows to exactly that residual, and is stronger for narrowing. Three locations repeating the un-narrowed claim are corrected to cite R1. **18. Explainability stays bounded to HTBW-governed participation, restating the existing capability/participation boundary, never a comprehensive recorder.** Configuration establishes which Persons, Rooms, capabilities, and entities are *eligible* for HTBW governance; actual *participation* in a specific governed evaluation determines what belongs in that evaluation's own trace. An entity's mere Room assignment or HTBW eligibility never causes trace capture for every one of its state changes; only its material participation as trigger, target, or evaluated input does. A native-caused change with no HTBW governed evaluation remains a Domain Event with behaviour attribution (**OD-63/DL-73**, **OD-64/DL-111**, both unchanged, neither absorbed here), never retroactively promoted into a Decision Trace | A second Explainability model, Recorder, Activity responsibility, or Activity store;
